Option

 |

Description

 |
 |

No option

 |

Starts the software in development mode online and shows the Setup perspective

 |
 |

`-o`

 |

Starts the software in development mode offline and shows the Setup perspective

 |
 |

`-E`

 |

(HPSmarTest -Eo for offline operation)

Starts the software in the production environment, with Engineer status. With this status, you can move back and forth freely between the development screens (where you develop a test program) and the production screens, and also to Supervisor and Operator status.

 |
 |

`-S`

 |

(HPSmarTest -So for offline operation)

Starts the software in the production environment, with Supervisor status. With this status, you only have access to the production screens. You can access the development screens by changing to Engineer status - provided you know the engineer password.

 |
 |

`-O`

 |

(HPSmarTest -Oo for offline operation)

Starts the software in the production environment, with Operator status. With this status, you can only select workorders, and execute them. You can access the development screens by changing to Engineer status - provided you know the engineer password.

 |
 |

`-C`

 |

(HPSmarTest -Co for offline operation)

Starts the software in the production environment, with Operator status and with the Operator Console. The workorder dialogs (the various texts for areas of the Workorder Select screens where you select something, or enter a particular value, Workorder Name, Lot_id, for example) also appear on the operator console.

 |
 |

-P

 |

(HPSmarTest -Po for offline operation)

Starts the software in the production environment in protected mode, which protects setup files against modification. This mode gives no access to any debug or setup GUI's, and does also not allow switching into any other mode (see [Protection for your setup files](<01.01.07.02.02.03_Protection_for_your_setup_files.md>)).

 |
 |

-v

 |

Show the current SmarTest version

 |
 |

-j

 |

Starts the software in the supervising mode, providing operation and supervising tools like the calibration data converter.

NOTE: Starts the software using the software license value package components only.

 |
 |

-n

 |

Starts the software without any licenses.

For installation or service that needs no software license value package components (compare option -j)

 |
 |

-?

 |

Shows a compact usage of the command `HPSmarTest`

 |

orig:
|

assemble

 |

Merges the subfiles specified in the master file of the master_file parameter and downloads the resulting setup file. The name of the target file is specified by the testerfile entry within the master file.

 |
 |

split

 |

Splits the tester setup file specified by the testerfile parameter within the master file into subfiles according to the entries in the master file.

If some parts of the tester setup file are not included in the entries of the master file, the setup management tool will generate the sub-files for these parts automatically. The naming strategy of the automatically generated sub-files are controlled by two macro variables, VERIGY93000_MFH_CONTENTBASED and VERIGY93000_MFH_PREFIX.

VERIGY93000_MFH_PREFIX defines the prefix to be used in the naming strategy.

VERIGY93000_MFH_CONTENTBASED defines the naming strategy. Its value can be 1, 0 or empty.

  - If VERIGY93000_MFH_CONTENTBASED is set to 1, the automatically generated sub-files will be named <prefix> eqnset_<equationNumber>. ("eqnset" is used if the content of the tester file is an equation set. The string to be used depends on the content of the tester file.) For example, to split a level tester file, if the prefix is "LEVEL" and two sub-files are automatically generated. These two files will be named LEVELeqnset_01.lev and LEVELeqnset_02.lev.
  - If VERIGY93000_MFH_CONTENTBASED is set to 0 or empty, the automatically generated sub-files will be named <prefix>mfh_generated_<fileNumber>. For example, to split a level tester file, if the prefix is "LEVEL" and two sub-files are automatically generated, these two files will be named LEVELmfh_generated_01.lev and LEVELmfh_generated_02.lev.
 |
 |

assemble_all

 |

Performs a merge for all master files in a device directory. If smartest_mfh is not called in the root directory of the device, the device directory must be specified in the last parameter.

 |
 |

split_all

 |

Performs a split for all master files in a device directory. If smartest_mfh is not called in the root directory of the device, the device directory must be specified in the last parameter.

 |
 |

create

 |

Creates an empty master file with the specified file name. The new file specifies the master file name without the .mfh extension as the tester setup file. If the tester setup file you want to split has a different name, you must either change the tester file name in the master file, or rename the tester setup file.

For this, and only for this, option you must specify the file_type parameter.

 |

|

Option

 |

Description

 |
 |

Resolve name conflicts by adding suffix automatically

 |

This option determines how to resolve name conflicts when you copy and paste nodes into a testflow.

- If you enable this option, the name of the pasted node is the original name with "_1" added at the end.
- If you disable this option, pasting a node opens the Name Conflict window prompting you to enter a new name for the pasted node.
 |
 |

Synchronize selection between [Flow Data Editor](<../../02_System_reference/02.08_Setup_and_Result_Tools/02.08.04.32.03.01_Flow_Data_Editor.md>) and [Flow Sequence Editor](<../../02_System_reference/02.08_Setup_and_Result_Tools/02.08.04.32.03.02_Flow_Sequence_Editor.md>)

 |

- If you enable this option, the display of the test component is synchronized between the two editors. For example, if you click a test suite in the Flow Sequence Editor, the test suite is also in focus in the Flow Data Editor.
- If you disable this option, the display of the test component is not synchronized between the two editors.
 |
 |

Synchronize selection between Debug view and Testflow editors

 |

- If you enable this option, when you execute the test suites one by one in the Debug view, the last executed test suite will be highlighted in the testflow tool.
- If you disable this option, the highlighted test suite in the testflow tool will not be changed with the execution in the Debug view.
 |
 |

Execute selected UTM Test Method as separate process (to avoid blocking)

 |

As the UTM CDT debugger is always attached to the default executor, the invocation of new Test Method is blocked if one Test Method is already suspended by the debugger.

By enabling this option, SmarTest always executes selected UTM Test Method on another executor as separate process. Its execution is no longer blocked.

Beware that those executions do not share the same process space. Value of global variable, for example, is different in each executor.

 |
 |

Check UTM test method library version when opening testflow editor

 |

- If you enable this option, when you open a testflow, the testflow tool will check whether the test method library is built on the version of SmarTest you are currently using. If not, a warning message will be displayed.
- If you disable this option, no checking of the test method library will be done when you open a testflow.
 |
 |

When running shmoo tests, warn that no shmoo plot will be generated

 |

This option determines how SmarTest behaves when you run a shmoo testflow using the Run Selected command.

- If you enable this option, SmarTest opens a window asking you whether you want to transfer the test suite or not.
- If you disable this option, SmarTest transfers the test suite without further notice.
 |
 |

Ask before copying testflow variables that do not exist in the target test flow.

 |

This option determines how SmarTest behaves when you [merge testflows](<../../02_System_reference/02.08_Setup_and_Result_Tools/02.08.04.32.02.05_Merging_the_testflows.md>) and at least one element of the source testflow contains a variable that does not exist in the target testflow:

- If you enable this option, SmarTest opens a window in which you decide whether SmarTest creates the variables with their default value in the target testflow or SmarTest does not copy those elements to and does not create the variables in the target testflow.
- If you disable this option, SmarTest copies the testflow elements and creates the variables with their default values automatically.
 |
 |

Startup options

 |

Specify whether the last opened editor (the Flow Data Editor or the Flow Sequence Editor) or both editors will be opened next time when you double-click the testflow item in the Test Program Explorer view.

 |

orig:
|

Environment Variable

 |

Description

 |
 |

AGILENT93000_PPUDEV

 |

Defines the RS-232 interface for pay per use:

- /dev/ttyS0: COM1
- /dev/ttyUSB0: Port 0 of USB to RS-232 adapter
- /dev/ttyUSB1: Port 1 of USB to RS-232 adapter
 Note

To identify the USB ports refer to the appropriate product guide:

Z4 G4: [Z4_Maintenance_Service_Guide.pdf](<../../../../pdf/Z4_Maintenance_Service_Guide.pdf>)

 |
 |

AGILENT93000_TMP_DIR

 |

Specifies the location of the SmarTest temporary directory. The default is under /var/opt/hp93000/soc/tmp

 |
 |

DATAFORMATTER_SYSTEM_CONFIG_DIRECTORY

 |

Specifies the location of the main configuration files of the data formatter. The default path is /etc/opt/hp93000/soc_common/datalog

 |
 |

DI_RS-232

 |

Used to specify the built-in RS-232 interface to use for diagnostics. By default, ttyUSB0 is used.

- ttyS0 COM1
- ttyUSB0 Port 0 of USB to RS-232 adapter
- ttyUSB1 Port 1 of USB to RS-232 adapter.
 Note

To identify the USB ports refer to the appropriate product guide:

Z4 G4: [Z4_Maintenance_Service_Guide.pdf](<../../../../pdf/Z4_Maintenance_Service_Guide.pdf>)

 |
 |

DISPLAY_HP83000

 |

This can be any name. You need to set this variable when running more than one SmarTest session on the same workstation.

 |
 |

GLOBAL_HANDLER_CONFIGURATION

 |

The default is normally /etc/opt/hp93000/soc/PH_libs/GenericHandler/Global-handler-config.cfg

This variable specifies the location of the 93000 handler configuration file, which specifies the handler model and configuration file.

 |
 |

GLOBAL_PROBER_CONFIGURATION

 |

The default is normally /etc/opt/hp93000/soc/PH_libs/GenericProber/Global-prober-config.cfg

This variable specifies the location of the 93000 prober configuration file, which specifies the prober model and configuration file.

 |
 |

HP83000_ANNOTATE_MCDLog

 |

Allows that the names of every testsuite are logged in the /var/opt/hp93000/soc/MCDLog.

This is very useful for debugging.Set this variable like this:export HP83000_ANNOTATE_MCDLog=1

You get easily turn on the MCDLog by running DIAG 2 from the hpt utility. DIAG -2 turns logging off (see [Using the Trace Function](<../../02_System_reference/02.06_Command_Reference/02.06.01.03.05_Using_the_Trace_Function.md>)).

 |
 |

HP83000_EDITOR

 |

The default editor under Linux is NEdit. If you prefer another editor like vi, you can specify HP83000_EDITOR=/bin/vi

 |
 |

HP83000_PRC_TIMEOUT

 |

Default of 30 seconds.This is the timeout value SmarTest uses when waiting for sub-processes to start. You may increase this value on systems with a very high load.

 |
 |

HP83000_ROOT

 |

Default is /opt/hp93000/soc

 |
 |

LANG

 |

Set it to C for a proper operation of the Pin Margin tool.

 |
 |

SA_NO_SPLASH

 |

Default is 0.

Set it to 1 to disable the appearance of the splash screen during SmarTest startup, see [How to disable the interactive windows](<../../02_System_reference/02.09_Test_Program_Management/02.09.01.16.01.01_How_to_disable_the_interactive_windows.md>).

 |
 |

SHOW_PROG_COMPONENTS

 |

Default is OFF.If you set this variable to ON, the Work Order Select screen will display another panel with additional details about the work order (test program, test flow etc.)

 |
 |

SOC_GPIB_SYSTEM_ONLINE

 |

If you want to use the Test Methods API for controlling GPIB instruments when SmarTest is off-line, set this variable to 1.

 |
 |

V93000_LICENSING

 |

Specifies the location of the device license file. The must location for the device license file is <device-directory>/license

 |
 |

V93000_MODEL

 |

Specifies the location of the model file. The default location for the model file is /etc/opt/hp93000/soc/model

 |
 |

WORKORDER_PATH

 |

Normally, work orders are located under `$HOME/workorders`.

This variable allows you to specify a different path for workorders.

 |

- Signal frequency:
 |

Digital signals are broadband.

 |
 |

- Current amplitude:
 |

The voltage drop is proportional to the signal current.

 |
 |

- Noise voltage threshold:
 |

The noise level a circuit can withstand or generate. For a cost effective design consider the acceptable noise level.

 |
 |

- Return path:
 |

At low frequencies current follows the path of least resistance. At high frequencies, current follows the path of least inductance (or, in more general terms: impedance).

Therefore you need to provide a direct low impedance / resistance return path, depending on high or low frequency requirements.

See also [Connecting the different grounds on the DUT board](<02.03.07.08.05.02_Connecting_the_different_grounds_on_the_DUT_board.md>).

 |
 |

- Multiple propagation paths
 |

The return current is distributed inversely proportional to the impedance of each path. Therefore, make sure to always provide only one return path right underneath (or nearby) the signal path (see also [Signal return paths](<02.03.07.01.09_Signal_return_paths.md>)). This applies to both horizontal layer paths and vertical layer paths.

|

Failure Case

 |

Impact on Test System

 |

Recovery

 |
 |

FLEXlm License Server Crash

 |

Systems that get their licenses from this server stop once they change device, reboot, calibrate, run diagnostic. Otherwise the testers keep running

 |

If Harddisk failure, repair Harddisk, install SW and existing licenses.

 |
 |

FLEXlm License Server Crash and Test Floor Network down

 |

Systems that get their licenses from this server stop once they change device, reboot, calibrate, run diagnostic. Otherwise the testers keep running

 |

Use ELF process on a Network outside Test Floor (for example, Internet Cafe) and obtain license. Use floppy disk, Flash card, any removable media, or print out license key and type in on test floor computers.

 |

Systems that get their licenses from this server stop once they change device, reboot, calibrate, run diagnostic. Otherwise the testers keep running

 |

No recovery until Advantest server is up again.

|

Data rates

 |

The Pin Scale 5000 digital card can handle data rates up to 5000 Mbit/s drive, receive and capture, given the prerequisites listed in [Pin Scale 5000 basic parameters](<../02.02_Specifications/02.02.04.03.01_Pin_Scale_5000_basic_parameters.md>).

 |
 |

Independent clock domains

 |

Independent clock domains per pin enable each pin to run at a different data rate. This allows:

- Unconstrained routing on the test fixture
- Concurrent testing of all interfaces at their native data-rates
- Optimized tester resource utilization with per pin granularity
- Each pin to synthesize its own and independent data-rate
 |
 |

Sequencer‑controlled board ADC

 |

One sequencer‑controlled ADC for high accuracy voltage measurements is provided for each channel module (Board ADC). This gives you 16 BADCs per PS5000 card, one BADC for 16 pins (see [Pin Scale 5000 hardware overview](<02.05.04.02.05_Pin_Scale_5000_hardware_overview.md>)).

 |
 |

Sequencer‑controlled pin PMU (PPMU)

 |

A sequencer‑controlled PPMU is provided for each pin for accurate current and voltage measurements (see [Pin Scale 5000 hardware overview](<02.05.04.02.05_Pin_Scale_5000_hardware_overview.md>)).

 |
 |

Pattern synchronous DC value measurements

 |

 Pattern synchronous DC value measurements (see [Pin Scale 5000 DC value measurements](<02.05.04.02.07.02_Pin_Scale_5000_DC_value_measurements.md>)) can be performed during the execution of a pattern using either the board ADC (BADC), the pin PMU (PPMU), or both depending on the accuracy you require. This feature is also referred to as sequencer‑controlled measurement of values.

 |
 |

Embedded timing search (fast adjustment)

 |

 [Embedded timing search (fast adjustment)](<02.05.04.02.03.02_Pin_Scale_5000_embedded_timing_search.md>) per-pin functionality allows you to adjust your timing to the actual behavior of the DUT. As this feature is embedded, it saves test time, as the data does not need to be uploaded to the workstation.

 |
 |

Preventing floating pins

 |

The active load should help to prevent a floating pin rather than a pull-down resistor.

 |

In the Measure dialog you cannot only set the standard parameters, but also switch a capacitance on the DUT board for the measurement.

The related utility pin, the target state of the pin, and the target capacitance can be defined in the Measure dialog:

   ![XPS256 HW view DPS Measure dialog](<../../../../raw/355120.png>) |

Several other fields that are marked in white can be changed in several sub‑dialogs.

An example for the other sub‑dialogs is the DPS Protection dialog that allows you changing parameters such as the maximum voltage drop or the status of the internal force to sense connection, which is named Open Loop Protection:

   ![XPS256 HW view DPS Protection dialog (355804)](<../../../../raw/355804.png>) |

edge_spec

 |

The edge specifier can either be a physical edge (d1 through d8 or r1 through r8), or one of the data parameters D1, D2, C1, C2 (drive parameters) or E1, E2 (receive parameters).

If you specify a physical edge, the dev_cyc_name and the dc_ref parameters must be omitted.

 |
 |

edge_number

 |

In the query reply, this parameter contains the edge that is used as leading or trailing edge.

 |
 |

dev_cyc_name

 |

Specifies the name of a logical device cycle that uses the data parameter given as the edge_spec. It must be defined for all pins in pinlist. If you do not enter a name in this parameter, the first device cycle in the device cycle table is used.

 |
 |

dc_ref

 |

This parameter specifies whether the leading or the trailing edge that is associated with the specified dev_cyc_name and dc_ref parameters is to be returned. The two options are LE (for "leading edge") and TE (for "trailing edge").

The leading edge is always the first edge that is associated with the specified data parameter within the specified device cycle,

The trailing edge is determined differently for drive and receive parameters:

- Drive parameter: The trailing edge is the first drive edge after the leading edge that performs a data or tri-state action.
- Receive parameter: If the action of the leading edge is an edge compare, leading and trailing edge will be identical. If it is the start action of a window compare, then the associated window close edge is the trailing edge.
 |
 |

direction

 |

This parameter can be in or out. If in is selected to define an input edge, then the edge_spec parameter must be D1, D2, C1, or C2. If out is selected to define a receiver edge, then the edge_spec parameter must be E1 or E2. If either in or out is selected along with an edge_spec parameter of 1,2...6, then a check is performed to ensure that the edges of all pins are in the required direction. If no entry is made in this parameter, the measuring edges of the pin in pinlist can have any direction or be unused.

reuse_flag

 |

- R: The returned edge is used in another device cycle.
- N: The returned edge is not used in another device cycle.
 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The parameters of the EDDC? command are applied to all pins named in this parameter. If more than one pin is used, the names must be separated by a comma.

In a multi-port setup, all pins must belong to the same port of the specification that was entered as the first parameter.

orig:
|

waveform_set

 |

Waveform Set Number. Enter PRM for the Primary Waveform Set, or an integer in the range 1 to the maximum number of allowed waveform sets. The maximum number is determined by [WSUS, WSUS? - (Waveform Sets USed)](<02.06.02.02.342_WSUS__WSUS__-__Waveform_Sets_USed.md>). For the query, you can also enter ALL for all waveform sets.

 |
 |

specset_id

 |

Derived as follows:

`100 *`equation_set_no `+ `specset_no

 |
 |

multi-port_spec

 |

For a multi-port setup, specify the name of a multi-port specification.

Note that the multi-port specification uniquely determines an equation set for every pin of pinlist, because no pin can belong to more than one port within a multi-port specification.

 |
 |

timing_set

 |

Timing Set Number. Enter PRM for the Primary Timing Set, ALL for all timing sets, or an integer in the range 1 to the maximum number of allowed timing sets. The maximum number is determined by TSUS.

 |
 |

mode

 |

The operating mode. For the query, you can enter ALL for all modes or BIDIR for bidirectional mode, that is, for edges that serve both as drive and receive edges.

With fast pins, you can specify the mode DELTA for both the command and the query. In this mode, the delays specified for edges with an index > 1 are interpreted as offsets from the calculated default values.

 |
 |

definition_string

 |

The definition string consists of a sequence of items each of which associates a delay with a drive or compare edge. On Pin Scale 800/3600 boards, drive edges are denoted by dn. On Pin Scale 9G boards, there are two kinds of drive edges, which are denoted by fn and sn, respectively; for details see [Defining waveforms for Pin Scale 9G pins](<02.06.06.01.03.02_Defining_waveform_shapes_for_Smart_Scale_pins.md>). You can also use the dn notation for Pin Scale 9G channels, but mixing both notations in one string is not allowed. Receive edges are always denoted by rn.

Unless you employ the pdiv statement for fast pins (see below), all edges which are not explicitly set remain unchanged.

The range of the edge delay is -8000 ns to +24000 ns (or -4 to +12 test system periods) for the Pin Scale 3600/800.

On Pin Scale 800/3600 boards, the restrictions for edge ordering must be observed both in fixed and equation based timing. For example, you cannot assign a greater delay to d1 than to d3 if d1 precedes d3 in a waveform definition. For more information, see [Selecting and ordering edges](<02.06.06.01.03.01.02_Selecting_and_ordering_edges.md>).

Note that with equation based timing, ETDS returns no error message when the edge order restrictions are violated.

On Pin Scale 9G boards, ordering of drive edges is not restricted in any way.

 |
 |

 |

Special Rules for Fast Pins:

If a pin is configured as a fast pin in the context of the specification given by the first parameter, you can specify the period divider at the start of the definition string. The format is pdiv:n, where n must be the same value as the period_div value of the pins in pinlist within the timing set specified by the timing_set parameter.

If you specify pdiv:nand a delay for the first edge, ETDS calculates delays for the following n-1 edges except those that are specified explicitly in the string. Note that for n = 3, the edges with index 1, 3, 5 are used for internal reasons.

If you omit either pdiv or the first edge, only the specified edges are modified. However, with receive edges this is only possible for r1.

The calculated delays are determined for the ith edge by the following formula:

 1st_edge_delay + (i-1) * (period/pdiv)

1st_edge_delay is the delay specified for the first edge (d1 or r1; the generic notation e1 is not allowed for fast pins). If the first edge is not specified in the string, its delay is set to 0. An example for the calculation will be given below.

Note that when both the period divider and a delay for the first edge are present in the definition string, then the delays for all the edges required by the period divider will be overwritten.

When a delay is explicitly specified for one of the edges, this delay overrides the calculated default. There are two formats to specify overrides. You can either define absolute delays or the offsets from the default delays.

term_mode

 |

The termination mode has dependencies to pin types and to the parameters (term_pulldown and param_1 to param_3 - see the syntax). The allowed combinations are shown in the Termination modes table, below.

Level set 0 only supports the termination modes OFF (the default), T, C, and A.

 |
 |

term_pulldown

 |

Extra parameter that defines the pull down mode. For more information refer to column term_mode of table Termination modes below.

The query returns the parameter only if it is defined for the queried level set.

 |
 |

param_1

 |

The use of this parameter depends on the termination mode as shown in the Termination modes table, below. When used, param_1 gives the termination voltage, active load commutation voltage, or the clamp low level voltage. The units are mV.

param_2

 |

The use of this parameter depends on the termination mode as shown in the Termination modes table, below. When used, param_2 defines the active load Iol current, or the clamp high level voltage. The units are mA or mV respectively.

When used, param_2 defines either

- the active load Iol current in µA,

- For term_mode = bidir_receiver, param_3 defines the receiver offset in mV.

l_range

This parameter can be

- I5E3: Defines the low current range of 0 to 5 mA.
- I3E4: Defines the high current range of 0 to 30 mA.

|

vec_No

 |

A logical vector number of the selected label. For the command, it determines the first active vector that will be overwritten.

For the query, this parameter specifies the vector at which analysis of the vector area starts (see also the description of the strt_disp parameter below).

 |
 |

dev_cyc_name

 |

Possible values are:

- The name of a defined device cycle.
- FDC: The first device cycle specifier. It indicates that the first device cycle in the device cycle table for the pins in pinlist is to be taken. If the length of this device cycle is not equal to the length parameter dev_cyc_len, an error is reported in the report window and the pins with this error are not set.

This specifier should be used only if you are working with device cycles consisting of just one test system cycle. The specifier gives you a shortcut to a device cycle name, where all device cycles have the same length (of 1).

 |
 |

dev_cyc_len

 |

The length of the specified device cycle.

For the query, the length specifies the analyzed range of active vectors, starting at the vector number vec_No. Enter an integer in the range 0 to 256 (see also the description of the disp_length parameter below).

 |
 |

ed_comp

 |

The edit component. This parameter is optional. It specifies which direction parameter (either Dx for drive or EDx for expected data, where x is 1 or 2) is being edited. The direction parameter being edited is fixed, and the system can, if necessary, auto-correct the other direction parameter.

The edit component can take the following values:

- dd1d: Drive data 1, drive value
- dd1z: Drive data 1, high-Z value
- dd2d: Drive data 2, drive value
- dd2z: Drive data 2, high-Z value
- ed1: Expected data 1 value
- ed2: Expected data 2 value

If the edit component is one of dd1d, dd1z, dd2d, or dd2z, then both the DD1 and DD2 parameters are fixed, and the ED1 and ED2 parameters can be auto-corrected to yield a consistent physical waveform sequence.

If the edit component is ed1 or ed2, then the ED1 and ED2 parameters are fixed, and the DD1 and DD2 parameters can be auto-corrected.

If no edit component parameter is specified, then all four direction parameters are fixed.

 |
 |

DD1

DD2

 |

Drive data parameters. They contain values for both drive data and tri-state. The values you can define are:

- F00: Drive 0, tri-state off
- F10: Drive 1, tri-state off
- F0Z: Drive 0, tri-state on
- F1Z: Drive 1, tri-state on
- N: Not used. Enter it if you do not want to set a drive data parameter to a drive and tri-state value.
- UC: Unclear. You must not enter this parameter value. The system may return this value as an answer to your query, to indicate that the interpretation of the device cycle for that parameter is unclear, that is, the physical waveforms are inconsistent for the device cycle. This response from the system is possible only if you do not use the Timing Setup to generate your device cycles.

The drive data parameters F0N, F1N, FN0, and FNZ, which set just the drive value or just the tri-state value (as is the case with the WAVE command), cannot be used here

 |
 |

ED1

ED2

 |

Expected data parameters. The values you can define are:

- F0: Compare to 0
- F1: Compare to 1
- FI: Compare to intermediate
- FX: Compare to mask
- FU: Compare to unstable
- N: Not used. Enter it if you do not want to set an expected data parameter to a compare value.
- UC: Unclear. You must not enter this parameter value. The system may return this value as an answer to your query, to indicate that the interpretation of the device cycle for that parameter is unclear, that is, the physical waveforms are inconsistent for the device cycle. This response from the system is possible only if you do not use the Timing Setup to generate your device cycles.
 |
 |

strt_disp

 |

This parameter defines the offset of your range of interest from vec_No. The actual display starts with the last device cycle that does not begin before vec_No and does not end before vec_No + strt_disp.

The purpose of this construction is to enable a correct device cycle reconstruction even if the first vector you are interested in does not lie at a device cycle boundary (a device cycle can span up to 16 vectors).

 |
 |

disp_length

 |

Specifies the display length in vectors. This parameter determines the end of your range of interest. The actual display ends with the last device cycle that starts before vec_No + strt_disp + disp_length.

 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The pin name or names for which a vector data transfer is to be made. If more than one pin is required, the names must be separated with a comma. Pins that do not belong to the port of the label are ignored.

|

connectionSet

 |

This parameter is currently not used.

This extra string parameter adds the ability to define several pins containing the same DC Scale channel in PMU mode. A multiple defined DC Scale channel can be sequentially reused as single pin or in ganging groups. Note: The documentation for supported DC Scale cards knows this feature also as "Ganging on the fly".

Default connection set: The default connection set is defined if this extra parameter is not used or if an empty string is programmed. A DC Scale pin can be defined in only one default connection set.

All traces that are needed for a cross-card ganging group and are defined by the [DDIC](<02.06.02.02.54_DDIC__DDIC__-__Define_DUT_Interface_Connection.md>) command and the DFPN command must have the same connectionSet defined. Recommendation: If the DUT trace can be activated by utility lines, name it like the utility line (see DFUP command).

There can be several pin definitions containing the same channel:

Adding a different ganging combination (new pin), does not invalidate the setups for the existing pins.

The different pins containing the same channel must be part of the same ports.

The patterns, events and DC-setups of these pins do not overlap.

 |
 | channelNo_1 |

The test system channel number of the channel to which the specified device pin is connected (five digits), or the utility block number of the specified card cage (three digit).

Digital or DC Scale channel

For a digital channel this is a five digit number. The first three digits specify the pogo block number, and the fourth and fifth digits specify the pin number in the pogo block. The first digit is 1 to 4, the second and third digits is 01 to 32, and the final two digits is 01 to 16. For example, 10105 is the digital channel whose pogo pin number is 05 in the pogo block 101.

Each pogo block contains 16 digital channels. The pogo block numbers are determined by the slots in which the channel boards are installed.

The first three digits are also called the board number of the logical channel board, and the last two digits are a channel number in the logical channel board, where each logical channel board contains 16 channels

Utility DC channel

For the utility DC pins, this is a three digit number, specifying the utility block of the card cage. The referenced utility pogo must be one which can be connected to the DC rail of the card-cage. To get the utility block number, add 164 (264 for the second utility line card on EXA Scale test systems) to the desired utility line block, such that for example utility block 4 has number 168. For compatibility with SmarTest 7.6x, "HPMU1" now maps to "UTIDC165" and so on (for Smart Scale test systems only).

For more information, see subtopics in [Pogo pin assignment - Utility pogo blocks](<../02.03_DUT_board_design_reference/02.03.06.08_Pogo_pin_assignment_-_Utility_pogo_blocks.md>).

The hardware knows 4 Utility DC channels (pogo pins): DC-force, DC-sense, ground-sense, and guard. But because they are referenced as a group, one pin name is sufficient to reflect all 4 channels.

 |
 |

DC_channel_list

 |

You can define ganging for a set of DC Scale channels in PMU mode by specifying a list of DC Scale channels, separated by commas and enclosed by parentheses. The channels must be physically adjacent on the same board.

Before cross-card ganging can be used, the connection must be enabled by command [DDIC](<02.06.02.02.54_DDIC__DDIC__-__Define_DUT_Interface_Connection.md>).

pinNo

pinName

If a list of more than one pin is required, the pin names must be separated by a comma. If you query a non-existent pin, the system returns nothing.

|

connectionSet

 |

This parameter is currently not used.

This extra string parameter adds the ability to define several pins containing the same DC Scale channel in PMU mode. A multiple defined DC Scale channel can be sequentially reused as single pin or in ganging groups. Note: The documentation for supported DC Scale cards knows this feature also as "Ganging on the fly".

Default connection set: The default connection set is defined if this extra parameter is not used or if an empty string is programmed. A DC Scale pin can be defined in only one default connection set.

All traces that are needed for a cross-card ganging group and are defined by the [DDIC](<02.06.02.02.54_DDIC__DDIC__-__Define_DUT_Interface_Connection.md>) command and the DFPN command must have the same connectionSet defined. Recommendation: If the DUT trace can be activated by utility lines, name it like the utility line (see DFUP command).

There can be several pin definitions containing the same channel:

Adding a different ganging combination (new pin), does not invalidate the setups for the existing pins.

The different pins containing the same channel must be part of the same ports.

The patterns, events and DC-setups of these pins do not overlap.

 |
 | channelNo_1 |

The test system channel number of the channel to which the specified device pin is connected (five digits), or the utility block number of the specified card cage (three digit).

Digital or DC Scale channel

For a digital channel this is a five digit number. The first three digits specify the pogo block number, and the fourth and fifth digits specify the pin number in the pogo block. The first digit is 1 to 4, the second and third digits is 01 to 32, and the final two digits is 01 to 16. For example, 10105 is the digital channel whose pogo pin number is 05 in the pogo block 101.

Each pogo block contains 16 digital channels. The pogo block numbers are determined by the slots in which the channel boards are installed.

The first three digits are also called the board number of the logical channel board, and the last two digits are a channel number in the logical channel board, where each logical channel board contains 16 channels

Utility DC channel

For the utility DC pins, this is a three digit number, specifying the utility block of the card cage. The referenced utility pogo must be one which can be connected to the DC rail of the card-cage. To get the utility block number, add 164 (264 for the second utility line card on EXA Scale test systems) to the desired utility line block, such that for example utility block 4 has number 168. For compatibility with SmarTest 7.6x, "HPMU1" now maps to "UTIDC165" and so on (for Smart Scale test systems only).

For more information, see subtopics in [Pogo pin assignment - Utility pogo blocks](<../02.03_DUT_board_design_reference/02.03.06.08_Pogo_pin_assignment_-_Utility_pogo_blocks.md>).

The hardware knows 4 Utility DC channels (pogo pins): DC-force, DC-sense, ground-sense, and guard. But because they are referenced as a group, one pin name is sufficient to reflect all 4 channels.

DC_channel_list

 |

You can define ganging for a set of DC Scale channels in PMU mode by specifying a list of DC Scale channels, separated by commas and enclosed by parentheses. The channels must be physically adjacent on the same board.

Before cross-card ganging can be used, the connection must be enabled by command [DDIC](<02.06.02.02.54_DDIC__DDIC__-__Define_DUT_Interface_Connection.md>).

If a list of more than one pin is required, the pin names must be separated by a comma. If you query a non-existent pin, the system returns nothing.

Default: 256

Maximum: 16384

Note that the total number of device cycles gets evenly divided between the combined number of waveform sets and wavetables. If you use the default values, then 256 device cycles divides into the total number of 32 [waveform sets and wavetables](<02.06.02.02.90_DSCP__DSCP__-__Define_System_Control_Parameter.md#_98578__row_waveform_set>) to give you 8 device cycles per waveform set/wavetable. If you choose values that do not divide evenly, then the number of device cycles will be rounded up to the next multiple of the [waveform_set](<02.06.02.02.90_DSCP__DSCP__-__Define_System_Control_Parameter.md#_98578__row_waveform_set>) parameter.

 |
 | devicecycle_set |

The devicecycle_set parameter is an integer that defines the maximum number of device cycle sets that you can create. Device cycle sets are needed for selective digital capture.

Default: 1

Maximum: 128

The dps_set parameter is an integer that defines the maximum number of DPS sets you can create.

Default: 32

Maximum: 256

The level_set parameter is an integer that defines the combined total of level sets for fixed and equation based levels that you can create.

Default: 32

Maximum: 256

 |

This parameter defines the precision with which the period resolution is calculated by the system. It has no effect on a user defined period resolution (using, for example, the period_res keyword in the equation set).

The default is 4, if the .technology file does not contain this parameter.

If it does, the value of the .technology file is the default.

This value is set to 9, the greatest possible value, when a device is created.

Default: 256

Maximum: 512

 |
 | timing_set |

The timing_set parameter is an integer that defines the maximum combined total of timing sets for fixed and equation based timing you can create.

Default: 256

Maximum: 999

The number of timing sets must be equal to or greater than the number of waveform sets, as there must be at least one timing set per waveform set.

The waveform_set parameter defines the maximum combined total of waveform sets (fixed timing) and wavetables (equation based timing) you can create. Thus, if you specify a value of 32, you could, for example, create 10 waveform sets and 22 wavetables.

Default: 32

Maximum: 128

The identification number of the level set (fixed levels) in which you want the levels to be included. The number must not exceed the maximum number of level sets allowed (as defined by the [DSCP](<02.06.02.02.90_DSCP__DSCP__-__Define_System_Control_Parameter.md>) command). Typing ALL in this field sets the levels for all existing level sets. Typing PRM sets the drive voltage levels for the primary level set.

 |

Used in equation based level setup. It is derived as follows:

100000 * equation_set_no + 1000 * specset_no + level_set_no

Note that if you use the command for an equation based level setup, you modify only the runtime values, not the value in the level set.

logic_0_level

An integer (in mV) which sets the low level voltage for the drive amplifier.

 |

logic_1_level

 |

An integer (in mV) which sets the high level voltage for the drive amplifier.

 |
 |

v3h_level

 |

Input (drive) 3rd level definition (high level voltage shift). The expression of this extra parameter must define a value in millivolts (mV).

This parameter is no longer used.

 |

range

 |

This extra parameter selects the drive range in mV:

- -8000.0 ... 8000.0 selects the 8 V range
- -30000.0 ... 30000.0 selects the 30 V range
- all other values select the -40 V ... +80 V range

level_set_no

 |

The identification number of the level set in which you want the definitions to be included. The number must not exceed the maximum number of level sets allowed (as defined by [DSCP](<02.06.02.02.90_DSCP__DSCP__-__Define_System_Control_Parameter.md>)) and the level sets used (as defined by [LSUS](<02.06.02.02.155_LSUS__LSUS__-__Level_Sets_USed.md>)). Entering ALL in this field sets the termination mode for all existing level sets (except level set 0). Entering PRM in this field defines the termination mode for the primary level set.

Standard level sets have a number > 0. Level set 0 is a dedicated level set for digital pins in high-Z state. For more information see [Defining a level set for sequencer state OFF](<02.06.05.01.05.05_Controlling_high-Z_behavior_of_digital_pins_while_the_sequencers_are_OFF.md>).

 |

term_mode

 |

The termination mode has dependencies to pin types and to the parameters (term_pulldown and param_1 to param_3 - see the syntax). The allowed combinations are shown in the Termination modes table, below.

Level set 0 only supports the termination modes OFF (the default), T, C, and A.

 |
 |

term_pulldown

 |

Extra parameter that defines the pull down mode. For more information refer to column term_mode of table Termination modes below.

The query returns the parameter only if it is defined for the queried level set.

 |
 |

param_1

 |

The use of this parameter depends on the termination mode as shown in the Termination modes table, below. When used, param_1 gives the termination voltage, active load commutation voltage, or the clamp low level voltage. The units are mV.

 |
 |

param_2

 |

The use of this parameter depends on the termination mode as shown in the Termination modes table, below. When used, param_2 defines the active load Iol current, or the clamp high level voltage. The units are mA or mV respectively.

When used, param_2 defines either

- the active load Iol current in µA,
- the clamp high level voltage in mV, or
- the receiver swing voltage in mV.

For the NP termination modes SP, SM, SEP, or SEM, param_2 defines the receiver threshold in mV.

 |

param_3

 |

- For term_mode = CT, param_3 defines the receiver offset in mV.
- For term_mode = bidir_receiver, param_3 defines the receiver offset in mV.
 |
 |

l_range

 |

For term_mode `=`A the low level current range.

This parameter can be

- I5E3: Defines the low current range of 0 to 5 mA.

pinlist

- Drive parameter: The trailing edge is the first drive edge after the leading edge that performs a data or tri-state action.

If either in or out is selected along with an edge_spec parameter of 1,2...6, then a check is performed to ensure that the edges of all pins are in the required direction. - R: The returned edge is used in another device cycle.
- N: The returned edge is not used in another device cycle.

pinlist

mode

With fast pins, you can specify the mode DELTA for both the command and the query. In this mode, the delays specified for edges with an index > 1 are interpreted as offsets from the calculated default values.

definition_string

The definition string consists of a sequence of items each of which associates a delay with a drive or compare edge. On Pin Scale 800/3600 boards, drive edges are denoted by dn. On Pin Scale 9G boards, there are two kinds of drive edges, which are denoted by fn and sn, respectively; for details see [Defining waveforms for Pin Scale 9G pins](<02.06.06.01.03.02_Defining_waveform_shapes_for_Smart_Scale_pins.md>). You can also use the dn notation for Pin Scale 9G channels, but mixing both notations in one string is not allowed. Receive edges are always denoted by rn.

Unless you employ the pdiv statement for fast pins (see below), all edges which are not explicitly set remain unchanged.

The range of the edge delay is -8000 ns to +24000 ns (or -4 to +12 test system periods) for the Pin Scale 3600/800.

On Pin Scale 800/3600 boards, the restrictions for edge ordering must be observed both in fixed and equation based timing. For example, you cannot assign a greater delay to d1 than to d3 if d1 precedes d3 in a waveform definition. For more information, see [Selecting and ordering edges](<02.06.06.01.03.01.02_Selecting_and_ordering_edges.md>).

Note that with equation based timing, ETDS returns no error message when the edge order restrictions are violated.

On Pin Scale 9G boards, ordering of drive edges is not restricted in any way.

 |

Special Rules for Fast Pins:

If a pin is configured as a fast pin in the context of the specification given by the first parameter, you can specify the period divider at the start of the definition string. The format is pdiv:n, where n must be the same value as the period_div value of the pins in pinlist within the timing set specified by the timing_set parameter.

If you specify pdiv:nand a delay for the first edge, ETDS calculates delays for the following n-1 edges except those that are specified explicitly in the string. Note that for n = 3, the edges with index 1, 3, 5 are used for internal reasons.

If you omit either pdiv or the first edge, only the specified edges are modified. However, with receive edges this is only possible for r1.

The calculated delays are determined for the ith edge by the following formula:

 1st_edge_delay + (i-1) * (period/pdiv)

1st_edge_delay is the delay specified for the first edge (d1 or r1; the generic notation e1 is not allowed for fast pins). If the first edge is not specified in the string, its delay is set to 0. An example for the calculation will be given below.

Note that when both the period divider and a delay for the first edge are present in the definition string, then the delays for all the edges required by the period divider will be overwritten.

When a delay is explicitly specified for one of the edges, this delay overrides the calculated default. There are two formats to specify overrides. You can either define absolute delays or the offsets from the default delays.

If you want to use the second, relative format, you must specify DELTA for the modeparameter. Note that you can also specify negative offsets in the DELTA mode.

In a multi-port setup, every pin must belong to a port of the specified specification.

- dd2d: Drive data 2, drive value

pinlist

If more than one pin is to be included, the names must be separated with a comma.

spec_type

 |

LEV to specify levels, or

 |
 |

spec_name

 |

A string of up to 64 alphanumeric characters (upper or lower case) enclosed in double quotes.

If you use the option @port`[`@UNCHANGED`]`, (see the port parameter), you must include this extension in the double quotes, too.

 |
 |

port

 |

In a multi-port setup, you can add a port name to the spec variable. This will have the effect that the value of the variable will be modified only for pins belonging to this port. This holds even if the variable has global scope for this port in the timing specification.

If you specify the spec variable without a port in a multi-port setup, its value will only be modified for a pin whose port has the spec variable set to global scope.

For more information on the scope of a variable see [Global and local scope of base variables](<02.06.06.01.05.03.01_Global_and_local_scope_of_base_variables.md>).

Note that if a port that is specified with the name of the variable it is this port on which the value of the variable will be modified. The setup pins have no influence on this.

If spec_name is used in the definition of the port period, this port will be temporarily used as the primary port. resolution

The smallest step size to be used in the search. Especially useful in a binary search of a range of floating point numbers, where the number of values between start and stop is infinite. The unit must be the same as defined with the spec.

res_spec

BANDWIDTH

 |

This refers to the behavior when the detailed error map is located in the external memory, and result recording was aborted due to a bandwidth overflow of the memory.

 |
 |

TIMEOUT

 |

This refers to the behavior in case of a sequencer timeout.

 |
 |

ERIM

 |

SmarTest issues an error message immediately after completion of the test. In case of a recording abort, this message reports the channels, pins, and sites of all channel groups on which recording was aborted.

In case of a sequencer timeout, a list of those channels is returned on which the timeout occurred.

 |
 |

FLIM

 |

This option is only allowed with TIMEOUT.

SmarTest reports the test as failed, that is, FTST? returns F. This is the default for TIMEOUT.

 |
 |

ERRQ

 |

This option is only allowed with BANDWIDTH.

SmarTest does not issue an error message immediately after completion of the test, but only if a channel which is involved in a recording abort is queried for result data. In this case again, the channels, pins, and sites of all channel groups on which recording was aborted will be reported. This is the default for BANDWIDTH.

 |
 |

FLRQ

 |

This option is only allowed with BANDWIDTH.

SmarTest does not issue any error message. If a channel of a group on which recording was aborted is queried for result data, all its cycles will be reported as failing.

This option can be used in a production environment if the result data is recorded in acquire failure mode, since if any data is recorded with this recording mode, the device must in fact have failed. Actually, recording will only be aborted in case of a massive fail on several pins.

|

Tester Controller

 |

Master controller of the GPIB. The tester controller usually controls the GPIB, and all peripheral devices on the GPIB are slaves to the tester controller. The tester controller is always address 21.

However, any other device can become the GPIB (active) controller if it is equipped to act as a controller, and control is passed to it by the tester controller. The tester controller is always the GPIB (active) controller at power-up.

 |
 |

Active Controller

 |

Present controller of the GPIB. At power-up or whenever InterFace Clear (IFC) is set to true by the tester controller, the tester controller is the active controller.

Under certain conditions, the tester controller may pass control to another device that is capable of managing the GPIB, and the active controller can then pass control to another controller or back to the tester controller. If the tester controller sets IFC to true, the tester controller immediately becomes the active controller.

 |
 |

Talker

 |

A device that has been authorized by the present active controller to place data onto the GPIB. Only one talker can be authorized at a time.

 |
 |

Listener

 |

Any device that has been programmed by the active controller to accept data from the GPIB. Any number of devices on the GPIB can be programmed by the active controller to listen simultaneously.

 |

Error Handler Type (TM::EXIT_TYPE)

 |

Description

 |
 |

ABORT_FLOW

 |

All sites that have not been binned yet will be aborted and binned to the otherwise bin.

The testflow execution ends after the current run. It needs user interaction to restart the next testflow execution.

 |
 |

EXIT_FLOW

 |

All sites of the current test suite, which are to be executed, are sent to the otherwise bin.

All other sites continue their normal flow logic. There is no termination at the end of the current testflow execution.

 |
 |

EXIT_TO_BIN

 |

A failing site of the current test suite is disconnected and sent to the otherwise bin. Test suite execution continues with the other sites. There is no termination at the end of the current testflow execution.

 |
 |

RETURN_TO_FLOW

 |

For the current test site the test method execution is terminated and the test suite is set to fail (continues a fail branch in case of a "run and branch" node). The test method will be called for all the remaining sites without any more special handling.

 |
 |

RETRY

 |

For the current test site the test method execution is retried after the current result is logged as unreliable.

 |
 |

INTERACTIVE

 |

A dialog box opens. You can select one of the above error handler actions in the dialog box interactively.

 |
 |

THROUGH

 |

The test method program execution is continued even if an error occurs. Note that this is valid only for GPIB and Computation API (GPIB_XXXX and DSP_XXXX).

 |
 |

NONE

 |

No exception is thrown. The previously installed exception handlers will be removed.

Timeout time of the measurement (test) in s. The default timeout is 360000 s.

O

timeout_info

 |

This parameter returns timeout information. It can only be used in combination with the timeout parameter.

The reply of timeout_info depends on whether it is used with or without the trigger_info parameter.

If trigger_info is not specified, timeout_info returns global timeout information. Possible return values are:

0: No timeout occurred on any site.

1: A timeout occurred on one site at least.

If trigger_info is also specified, timeout_info returns site specific timeout information.

In this case, the returned integer must be converted into binary format. Every bit returns the timeout status of one site. Site 1 is represented by the LSB.

For example, if 13 is returned to this parameter, this corresponds to binary number 1101. This indicates that a timeout occurred on the site 1, site 3 and site 4.

 |
 |

O

 |

trigger_info

 |

This parameter returns site specific information on the trigger status of the digitizers. It can only be used in combination with the timeout_info parameter.

The reply refers to the following digitizers: MCA-ADGT/VDGT, MCB LF/VHF-DGT, and MCC. The state of the module (or MCA/MCB/MCC unit) is checked if a pin is defined and connected to the core.

The parameter informs about which of these digitizers have not been triggered from when the test is started by the NB_DIGITAL_CAPTURE_START API until the end of this API. For more details of this functionality, see [Error Handling on Missing Trigger Input](<02.07.03.16.03_Error_Handling_on_Missing_Trigger_Input.md>).

The returned integer must be converted into binary format. Every bit returns the trigger status of one site. Site 1 is represented by the LSB. The bit states have the following meaning:

0: All the digitizer/sampler modules (and all the MCA/MCB/MCC measure units) on the site have been triggered at least once.

1: At least one digitizer/sampler module (or one MCA/MCB/MCC measure unit) on the site has never been triggered (missed a trigger).

In offline mode, this flag indicates whether the trigger signal input is enabled for all the modules (and all the MCA/MCB/MCC units) (0) or not (1).

For example, if you make this API waited until AWGs and digitizers/samplers complete the current sequencer programs, specify TM::WAIT_AWG|TM::WAIT_DGT to this parameter.

waits until all used AWGs complete the current sequencer programs.

- TM::WAIT_DGT:

waits until all used digitizers and samplers complete the current sequencer programs.

- TM::WAIT_TIA:

waits until all used TIAs complete the current measurements..

Error Handler Type (TM::EXIT_TYPE)

 |

Description

 |
 |

ABORT_FLOW

 |

All sites that have not been binned yet will be aborted and binned to the otherwise bin.

The testflow execution ends after the current run. It needs user interaction to restart the next testflow execution.

 |
 |

EXIT_FLOW

 |

All sites of the current test suite, which are to be executed, are sent to the otherwise bin.

All other sites continue their normal flow logic. There is no termination at the end of the current testflow execution.

 |
 |

EXIT_TO_BIN

 |

A failing site of the current test suite is disconnected and sent to the otherwise bin. Test suite execution continues with the other sites. There is no termination at the end of the current testflow execution.

 |
 |

RETURN_TO_FLOW

 |

For the current test site the test method execution is terminated and the test suite is set to fail (continues a fail branch in case of a "run and branch" node). The test method will be called for all the remaining sites without any more special handling.

 |
 |

RETRY

 |

For the current test site the test method execution is retried after the current result is logged as unreliable.

 |
 |

INTERACTIVE

 |

A dialog box opens. You can select one of the above error handler actions in the dialog box interactively.

 |
 |

THROUGH

 |

The test method program execution is continued even if an error occurs. Note that this is valid only for GPIB and Computation API (GPIB_XXXX and DSP_XXXX).

 |
 |

NONE

 |

No exception is thrown. The previously installed exception handlers will be removed.

timeout_info

 |

This parameter returns timeout information. It can only be used in combination with the timeout parameter.

The reply of timeout_info depends on whether it is used with or without the trigger_info parameter.

If trigger_info is not specified, timeout_info returns global timeout information. Possible return values are:

0: No timeout occurred on any site.

1: A timeout occurred on one site at least.

If trigger_info is also specified, timeout_info returns site specific timeout information.

The returned integer must be converted into binary format. Every bit returns the timeout status of one site. Site 1 is represented by the LSB.

For example, if 13 is returned to this parameter, this corresponds to binary number 1101. This indicates that a timeout occurred on the site 1, site 3 and site 4.

 |
 |

O

trigger_info

 |

This parameter returns site specific information on the trigger status of the digitizers. It can only be used in combination with the timeout_info parameter.

The reply refers to the following digitizers: MCA-ADGT/VDGT, MCB LF/VHF-DGT, and MCC. The state of the module (or MCA/MCB/MCC unit) is checked if a pin is defined and connected to the core.

The parameter informs about which of these digitizers have not been triggered during execution of this API. For more details of this functionality, see [Error Handling on Missing Trigger Input](<02.07.03.16.03_Error_Handling_on_Missing_Trigger_Input.md>).

0: All the digitizer/sampler modules (and all the MCA/MCB/MCC measure units) on the site have been triggered at least once.

1: At least one digitizer/sampler module (or one MCA/MCB/MCC measure unit) on the site has never been triggered (missed a trigger).

I/O

 |

Parameter

 |

Description / Range

 |
 |

I

 |

timeout

 |

Timeout time of the measurement (test) in sec.

This cannot detect a timeout for the AWGs. Operations when timeout occurs depend on whether the timeout_info parameter is set or omitted. See Important Points.

 |
 |

O

 |

timeout_info

 |

This parameter returns timeout information. It can only be used in combination with the timeout parameter.

The reply of timeout_info depends on whether it is used with or without the trigger_info parameter.

If trigger_info is not specified, timeout_info returns global timeout information. Possible return values are:

0: No timeout occurred on any site.

1: A timeout occurred on one site at least.

If trigger_info is also specified, timeout_info returns site specific timeout information.

In this case, the returned integer must be converted into binary format. Every bit returns the timeout status of one site. Site 1 is represented by the LSB.

For example, if 13 is returned to this parameter, this corresponds to binary number 1101. This indicates that a timeout occurred on the sites 1, 3, and 4.

 |
 |

O

 |

trigger_info

 |

This parameter returns site specific information on the trigger status of the digitizers. It can only be used in combination with the timeout_info parameter.

The reply refers to the following digitizers: MCA-ADGT/VDGT, MCB LF/VHF-DGT, and MCC. The state of the module (or MCA/MCB/MCC unit) is checked if a pin is defined and connected to the core.

The parameter informs about which of these digitizers have not been triggered from when the test is started by the START_TEST API until the end of this API. For more details of this functionality, see [Error Handling on Missing Trigger Input](<02.07.03.16.03_Error_Handling_on_Missing_Trigger_Input.md>).

The returned integer must be converted into binary format. Every bit returns the trigger status of one site. Site 1 is represented by the LSB. The bit states have the following meaning:

0: All the digitizer/sampler modules (and all the MCA/MCB/MCC measure units) on the site have been triggered at least once.

1: At least one digitizer/sampler module (or one MCA/MCB/MCC measure unit) on the site has never been triggered (missed a trigger).

In offline mode, this flag indicates whether the trigger signal input is enabled for all the modules (and all the MCA/MCB/MCC units) (0) or not (1).

 |
 |

I

 |

wait_action

 |

This parameter allows you to select which sequencer's completion the API waits for, from the following hardware categories that are represented by the constant variables. It is also valid for combination of them by using "|" (use bitwise OR to select multiple ones). For example, if you make this API waited until AWGs and digitizers/samplers complete the current sequencer programs, specify TM::WAIT_AWG|TM::WAIT_DGT to this parameter.

Default: TM::WAIT_DIGITAL| TM::WAIT_DGT| TM::WAIT_TIA

- TM::WAIT_ALL

waits until all used digital channels, AWGs, digitizers/samplers, and TIAs complete their tasks.

- TM::WAIT_DIGITAL

waits until all used digital channels complete the current sequencer program.

- TM::WAIT_AWG

waits until all used AWGs complete the current sequencer programs.

- TM::WAIT_DGT

waits until all used digitizers and samplers complete the current sequencer programs.

- TM::WAIT_TIA

waits until all used TIAs complete the current measurements.

- TM::WAIT_TMU

waits until all running TMUs have finished their measurements.

 |
 |

I

 |

context

 |

Name of an execution context. The ports of the context must be included in the current start label (which must be a multiport burst). For more information on execution contexts see [Using execution contexts](<../02.06_Command_Reference/02.06.07.01.08.05.03.02.03_Using_execution_contexts.md>) .

The context must have been defined on the firmware level (with the [SQEC](<../02.06_Command_Reference/02.06.02.02.231_SQEC__SQEC__-__SeQuencer_Execution_Context.md>) command), or as a [SEQUENCER_CONTEXT_ITEM](<02.07.04.01.202_SEQUENCER_CONTEXT_ITEM.md>) object. In the latter case this object must have been included in a [SEQUENCER_CONTEXT](<02.07.04.01.201_SEQUENCER_CONTEXT.md>) object, and must also have been activated on the firmware level with the apply() function of this SEQUENCER_CONTEXT object. If the context has been defined as a SEQUENCER_CONTEXT_ITEM object, you must use the name specified for its name parameter.

 |
 |

I

 |

pins

If WAIT_TMU is included in the wait_action parameter, WAIT_TEST_DONE will by default wait until the TMU measurement has been completed on all pins of the active TMU set. With the pins parameter, this behavior can be restricted to the specified pins.

I

This parameter allows you to wait and abort the test execution, when a digital compare failure has happened. With the following options, users can

abort when the failure detected on all the pins.

abort when the failure detected on any of the listed pins.

waits until all used digital channels complete the current sequencer program.

waits until all used AWGs complete the current sequencer programs.

- TM::WAIT_TIA:

Attributes

 |

Definitions

 |
 |

searchType

 |

The available search types are:

- DIGITAL_OFFSET_SEARCH::EYE (default)
- DIGITAL_OFFSET_SEARCH::LB
- DIGITAL_OFFSET_SEARCH::RB

See the descriptions of each type in [DIGITAL_OFFSET_SEARCH_PINS.searchType()](<02.07.04.01.36.01.21_DIGITAL_OFFSET_SEARCH_PINS.searchType.md>).

 |
 |

resourceType

 |

The resource types for level searches are: VIH, VIL, VOH, VOL, VTH, VISWING, and VOSWING.

The resource types for timing searches are: DRIVE, RECEIVE, FAST_DRIVE, SLOW_DRIVE, and ALL_EDGES.

See the descriptions of each type in [DIGITAL_OFFSET_SEARCH_PINS.resourceType()](<02.07.04.01.36.01.18_DIGITAL_OFFSET_SEARCH_PINS.resourceType.md>).

 |
 |

start

 |

A value represents the interval between the search start and the value of the searched [resources](<02.07.04.01.36.01.18_DIGITAL_OFFSET_SEARCH_PINS.resourceType.md>). Negative values are allowed.

Therefore, the start position is calculated from:

(The value of the searched resource) + (The value set for this parameter).

The units for timing and voltage searches are [s] and [V].

 |
 |

numSteps

 |

The number of search steps excluding the start value for a timing or level offset search

 |
 |

stepWidth

 |

The step width for a timing or level offset search.

 |
 |

resolution (optional)

 |

The resolution for a binary search.

 |
 |

minPassCount (optional)

 |

A minimum consecutive pass count, which will stop the binary search if the consecutive pass count is equal to or greater than the minimum count.

 |
 |

transitionDetection (optional)

 |

The transition detection types are:

- DIGITAL_OFFSET_SEARCH::PF (default)
- DIGITAL_OFFSET_SEARCH::ECL

See the descriptions of each type in [DIGITAL_OFFSET_SEARCH_PINS.transitionDetection()](<02.07.04.01.36.01.27_DIGITAL_OFFSET_SEARCH_PINS.transitionDetection.md>).

 |
 |

errorCountLimit (optional)

 |

An error count limit is used to consider a test pass or fail. If the error count of a test is greater than this limit, the test is considered fail.

 |
 |

minStableErrorCount (optional)

 |

A minimum error count is used to measure a stable search.

If some adjacent tests have the same number of errors, and the number of these adjacent tests is equal to or greater than this minimum count, the search is regarded as stable.

 |
 |

resolutionHistogramSearch (optional)

 |

The step width for the histogram based search.

 |
 |

restoreFlag (optional)

 |

It can be:

- DIGITAL_OFFSET_SEARCH::YES: Enables the restore flag. The actual offsets will keep the original offsets before the searches.
- DIGITAL_OFFSET_SEARCH::NO: Disables the restore flag. The actual offsets will change to the searched offsets.
 |
 |

enableFastStop

 |

TRUE or FALSE to enable or disable the FASTSTOP mode.

To learn FASTMODE, refer to [DIGITAL_OFFSET_SEARCH_PINS.enableFastStop()](<02.07.04.01.36.01.02_DIGITAL_OFFSET_SEARCH_PINS.enableFastStop.md>).

mode

Test mode to be selected from the following items:

TM::GPF - Executes a Global Pass/Fail test which records a judgment of all pins. The result can be retrieved with the getPassFail() member function.

TM::PPF - Executes Per pin Pass/Fail tests which record judgments per pin. The results can be retrieved with the getPassFail(pin) member function.

TM::PVAL - Executes Per pin Value tests which records measured values per pin. The results can be retrieved with the getValue() member function.

TM::DCTEST_AUTO - Executes the DC test according to the test suite flags.

If the flag Pass value or Fail value is on, the DC test will executes in the same way as the mode TM::PVAL.

If the flag Pass value and Fail value are off and the flag Per pin on pass or Per pin on fail is on, the DC test will executes in the same way as the mode TM::PPF.

|

Error Handler Type (TM::EXIT_TYPE)

 |

Description

 |
 |

ABORT_FLOW

 |

All sites that have not been binned yet will be aborted and binned to the otherwise bin.

The testflow execution ends after the current run. It needs user interaction to restart the next testflow execution.

 |
 |

EXIT_FLOW

 |

All sites of the current test suite, which are to be executed, are sent to the otherwise bin.

All other sites continue their normal flow logic. There is no termination at the end of the current testflow execution.

 |
 |

EXIT_TO_BIN

 |

A failing site of the current test suite is disconnected and sent to the otherwise bin. Test suite execution continues with the other sites. There is no termination at the end of the current testflow execution.

 |
 |

RETURN_TO_FLOW

 |

For the current test site the test method execution is terminated and the test suite is set to fail (continues a fail branch in case of a "run and branch" node). The test method will be called for all the remaining sites without any more special handling.

 |
 |

timeout

Timeout time of the measurement (test) in sec. The default is 360000 s.

This cannot detect a timeout for the AWGs. Operations when timeout occurs depend on whether the timeout_info or trigger_info parameter is set or omitted.

 |
 |

O

 |

timeout_info

 |

This parameter returns timeout information. It can only be used in combination with the timeout parameter.

The reply of timeout_info depends on whether it is used with or without the trigger_info parameter.

If trigger_info is not specified, timeout_info returns global timeout information. Possible return values are:

0: No timeout occurred on any site.

1: A timeout occurred on one site at least.

If trigger_info is also specified, timeout_info returns site specific timeout information.

In this case, the returned integer must be converted into binary format. Every bit returns the timeout status of one site. Site 1 is represented by the LSB.

For example, if 13 is returned to this parameter, this corresponds to binary number 1101. This indicates that a timeout occurred on sites 1, 3, and 4.

 |
 |

O

 |

trigger_info

 |

This parameter returns site specific information on the trigger status of the digitizers. It can only be used in combination with the timeout_info parameter.

The reply refers to the following digitizers: MCA-ADGT/VDGT, MCB LF/VHF-DGT, and MCC. The state of the module (or MCA/MCB/MCC unit) is checked if a pin is defined and connected to the core.

The parameter informs about which of these digitizers have not been triggered during execution of this API. For more details of this functionality, see [Error Handling on Missing Trigger Input](<02.07.03.16.03_Error_Handling_on_Missing_Trigger_Input.md>).

The returned integer must be converted into binary format. Every bit returns the trigger status of one site. Site 1 is represented by the LSB. The bit states have the following meaning:

0: All the digitizer/sampler modules (and all the MCA/MCB/MCC measure units) on the site have been triggered at least once.

1: At least one digitizer/sampler module (or one MCA/MCB/MCC measure unit) on the site has never been triggered (missed a trigger).

In offline mode, this flag indicates whether the trigger signal input is enabled for all modules (and all the MCA/MCB/MCC units) (0) or not (1).

 |
 |

wait_action

 |

This parameter allows you to select which sequencer's completion the API waits for, from the following hardware categories that are represented by the constant variables. It is also valid for combination of them by using "|" (use bitwise OR to select multiple ones).

For example, if you make this API waited until AWGs and digitizers/samplers complete the current sequencer programs, specify TM::WAIT_AWG|TM::WAIT_DGT to this parameter.

Default:

TM::WAIT_DIGITAL| TM::WAIT_DGT| TM::WAIT_TIA

- TM::WAIT_ALL:

waits until all used digital channels, AWGs, digitizers/samplers, and TIAs complete their tasks.

- TM::WAIT_DIGITAL:

waits until all used digital channels complete the current sequencer program.

- TM::WAIT_AWG:

waits until all used AWGs complete the current sequencer programs.

- TM::WAIT_DGT:

waits until all used digitizers and samplers complete the current sequencer programs.

- TM::WAIT_TIA:

waits until all used TIAs complete the current measurements.

context

Category

   | Description |
 | General  | A new testflow variable RDI_CONFIGURE_FILE can specify a customized RDI_Configure file for each testflow. See [RDI_Configure file](<02.07.13.04_RDI_Configure_file.md>). |
 | Alarm handling for DCVI  | SmartRDI provides a solution for [alarm handling for DCVI](<02.07.13.09_SmartRDI__Alarm_handling_for_DCVI.md>) to ensure that force voltage or force current on device pins are as correct as expected.

SmartRDI provides [alarm checking commands](<02.07.13.09.02_Alarm_handling_commands.md>) to specify alarm sets, enable or disable alarm checking on pins, and set limit values.

Two keywords are introduced to activate the alarm handling in the RDI_Configure file:

- ALARM_HANDLING_DCVI_ENABLE: Enable the alarm handling for DCVI.
- ALARM_HANDLING_DCVI_SETUP_FILE: Specify a path that directs to an alarm setup file which contains the limit setups for handling alarms for DCVI pins.

See [SmartRDI: Alarm handling for DCVI](<02.07.13.09_SmartRDI__Alarm_handling_for_DCVI.md>) for more detailed information.

 |
 | DC Scale FVI16 card  | The FVI16 card is a high-current and high-voltage floating VI source that is optimized for a wide range of analog power tests. The card belongs to the DC Scale family and can reside in any channel card slot. |
 | ROUTE  | Two new functions are introduced in the route() class:

- [rdi.route().enableOnlyActiveSites()](<02.07.13.15.05.03_rdi.route__.enableOnlyActiveSites.md>) enables the utility line and PMUX switch settings on active sites or disables them on inactive sites.
 |
 | UTIL |

- The keyword UTIL_PADDING_RPTV_FLAT can be added in the [RDI_Configure file](<02.07.13.04_RDI_Configure_file.md>) for defining how many vectors are to be repeated in padding. The default value is 16.
- Utility control patterns take dvc "0" as 0, dvc "1" as 1, and dvc "Z" as Z in the util() class as in the route() class from this version.Note This change may cause a compatibility issue in existing test programs when running in SmartRDI 7.5.0. If util() commands do not work after you have switched to SmartRDI 7.5.0, check the index style.
 |
