- Put RDI_INFO_LEVEL message to a log file

See the new keyword ENABLE_RDI_INFO_LOG_FILE in [RDI_Configure file](<02.07.13.04_RDI_Configure_file.md>).

General Improvements:

- SmartVec upload speed improvement

  - Before SmartRDI 2.4.5, the DIGCAP read mode uploads data at a speed of 1 bit per word; SmartRDI 2.4.5 improves this speed to 32 bit per word.
  - In SmartRDI 2.4.5, the Emap read mode's upload speed is accelerated by [changing the default error map location](<02.07.13.16.02_emapLocation.md>). This improvement takes effect only if [the Emap location is set to RAM (default)](<02.07.13.04_RDI_Configure_file.md>).

- TMU upload speed improvement

In SmartRDI 2.4.5, the result upload of TMU pins with the same setup is combined. Because data upload for multiple TMU pins with the same parameters in one `RDI_BEGIN()/RDI_END()` block is combined, the upload speed is improved.

- 1st run speed improvement for non-MD5 bursts (SmarTest 7.4.2)

See BURST_NAME_MD5 in [RDI_Configure file](<02.07.13.04_RDI_Configure_file.md>).

- Label content checking with customized label name (SmarTest 7.4.2)

See the new keyword USER_NAMED_LABEL_CONTENT_CHECK in [RDI_Configure file](<02.07.13.04_RDI_Configure_file.md>).

 |
 |

SMC

 |

- Common thread SMC for error map result

Since SmartRDI 2.4.5, the error map result supports common thread SMC. See [Using SmartCalc (SMC) with SmartRDI](<02.07.13.08.19_Using_SmartCalc__SMC__with_SmartRDI.md>) and [rdi.site()](<02.07.13.08.19.02.04_rdi.site.md>).

- Non-SMC execution for short bursts

See the new keyword DISABLE_SMC_EXEC_SHORT_BURST in [RDI_Configure file](<02.07.13.04_RDI_Configure_file.md>).

- Flexible control of the SMC execution (global ON/OFF)

By default all `RDI_BEGIN()/RDI_END()` blocks run in the "SMC execution" mode, which can trigger result hidden upload of the previous tests, and take a longer time (extra 50-100 us) to complete compared to the normal execution. SmartRDI 2.4.5 provides two options to disable the default "SMC execution" mode.

  - A RDI_Configure option as a global setting of the mode. See the new keyword DISABLE_SMC_EXEC_GLOBAL in [RDI_Configure file](<02.07.13.04_RDI_Configure_file.md>).
  - A pair of commands to set the execution mode for the following `RDI_BEGIN()/RDI_END()` blocks in code. See the new topics [rdi.disableSmcExec()](<02.07.13.08.19.02.01_rdi.disableSmcExec.md>) and [rdi.enableSmcExec()](<02.07.13.08.19.02.02_rdi.enableSmcExec.md>).

- Improved code structure for SMC

  - In SmartRDI 2.4.5, `rdi.site().id().getXXX()` can be called anywhere inside a test method's `run()` function. See [rdi.site()](<02.07.13.08.19.02.04_rdi.site.md>).
  - In SmartRDI 2.4.5, `SMC_DISABLE(true)` can be combined with `rdi.hiddenUpload(TA::ALL)`. See [rdi.hiddenUpload()](<02.07.13.08.19.02.03_rdi.hiddenUpload.md>).

 |
 |

SmartVec

 |

- Auto burst upload for SmartVec digital capture

See the new keyword SMV_DIGCAP_AUTO_BURSTUPLOAD in [RDI_Configure file](<02.07.13.04_RDI_Configure_file.md>).

- `burstLabel()` with ports including `portSync()`

See "Example 5" in [burstLabel()](<02.07.13.24.03_burstLabel.md>).

- `labelName()` with MD5 postfix

See the new parameter TA::MD5_OPTION in [labelName()](<02.07.13.24.23_labelName.md>).

 |
 |

DC

 |

- Pattern‑based `loadCap()` change for AVI64

Minimum load capacity allowed changes from 1 uF to 1 nF, to fix the "Load Capacity value out of range" issue (CR-110587). See [loadCap()](<02.07.13.12.02.26_loadCap.md>).

 |
 |

Emap

 |

- Xmode support

See the new topic [xMode()](<02.07.13.16.12_xMode.md>).

 |
 |

UTIL

 |

- Utility mask for sequencer‑controlled utility lines

See the new keywords UTIL_DYN_MASK_UNSPECIFIED_PIN and UTIL_DYN_MASK_INACTIVE_SITE in [RDI_Configure file](<02.07.13.04_RDI_Configure_file.md>).

See also the new topic [Sequencer Controlled Utility Mask with SmartRDI](<02.07.13.23.04_Sequencer_Controlled_Utility_Mask_with_SmartRDI.md>).

 |
 |

portSync

 |

- portSync with the CTIM (Chang TIMing) instruction

See the new parameter TA::MD5_CTIM in [portSync()](<02.07.13.08.08.02_portSync.md>).

 |
 |

TMU

 |

- Timeout behavior improvement

Before SmartRDI 2.4.5, the TMU time out is set to 50 ms, which means that if the digital TMU does not get all results, it will wait for 50 ms after the pattern is finished. In SmartRDI 2.4.5, the timeout of the digital TMU is set to 0 ms, which means that the TMU stops working after the pattern is finished. To keep the same timeout behavior as SmarTest 2.4.4, a flag is implemented in the RDI_Configure file.

See the new keyword TMU_TIMEOUT_50ms in [RDI_Configure file](<02.07.13.04_RDI_Configure_file.md>).

 |
 |

Support

 |

- Return the RDI revision that TM code is built with

See the new topics [rdi.getActiveRdiRev()](<02.07.13.08.06.03_rdi.getActiveRdiRev.md>) and [rdi.getCompileRdiRev()](<02.07.13.08.06.04_rdi.getCompileRdiRev.md>).

Note This mode requires a pattern length not less than eight cycles for patterns inside a `RDI_BEGIN()`/`RDI_END()` block, because in BFLM mode, each pattern in the burst must generate eight or more cycles (see [Compression factor for overview Error Map](<../02.06_Command_Reference/02.06.11.01.02.01.02.07_Compression_factor_for_overview_Error_Map.md>)). So when this mode is enabled, a specified pattern length less than eight cycles is ignored and all patterns generated by SmartRDI have at least eight cycles. There are exceptions, for example `vecLength()` of the `smartVec()` class, where SmartRDI reports an error for a user setting with insufficient pattern length, rather than ignoring the setting. User labels less than eight cycles cause an error as well. |

| Keyword  | Description |
 | DEFAULT_EMAP_LOCATION  | Provide a global option to set an error map location:

- TP indicates an error map location in the test processor memory of the channel.
- RAM indicates that the error map is located in the vector memory of the channel.

If not specified, the default error map location is RAM, which is the vector memory, because this location provides a higher upload speed.

In case the vector memory is insufficient for the test, the location switches to TP, which is the test processor memory.

Note that the RAM location is related to the "result area" configuration in the technology file of SmarTest.

For information about the error map size, refer to [Pin Scale 1600 error map size](<../02.05_Test_Head_Cards/02.05.04.01.03.02_PS1600_error_map_size.md>).

See also [emapLocation()](<02.07.13.16.02_emapLocation.md>).Note TP is the default value before SmartRDI 2.4.5. RAM is the default value since SmartRDI 2.4.5. |
 | DEFAULT_SMV_READ_MODE  | Specify a central selection of SmartVec read mode for the whole test program: EMAP or DIGCAP.

If not specified, the default read mode is DIGCAP.

 |
 | SMV_DIGCAP_AUTO_BURSTUPLOAD  | Specify TRUE or FALSE to enable or disable automatic burst of upload.

The default value is TRUE.

Using [burstUpload](<02.07.13.13.06_burstUpload.md>) for data read by SmartVec in the digital capture mode can significantly decrease test time. By default, all SmartVec's digital capture data on a certain pin in one `RDI_BEGIN()/RDI_END()` block are uploaded as one burst, and the `burstUpload()` function set in the code is ignored.

The only exception is a combination of `digCap()` and `smartVec()` readings in the same `RDI_BEGIN()/RDI_END()` block on the same pin. As the digCap class supports different capture modes (par, ser, bitPerWord), the smartVec burstUpload will be split into segments between the digCap commands.

 |
 | SMV_VEC_MEM_TYPE  | Specify the memory location to put generated smartVec patterns: SHMEM or SM.

If not specified, SM is used by default.

 |
 | USER_NAMED_LABEL_CONTENT_CHECK  | Specify TRUE or FALSE to enable or disable whether to check label content when you set a label name.

The default value is TRUE.

Based on [the new LBUD firmware command in SmarTest 7.4.2](<../02.06_Command_Reference/02.06.02.02.154_LBUD__LBUD__-__LaBel_User_Data.md>), this option provides a capability of performing a content check on labels set by one of the following commands or command combinations:

- A `labelName()` function in the `smartVec()` class
- A `burstLabel(TA::MD5_OFF)` function in the `smartVec()` class
- A `label().copyLabel(false)` function combination in the `dc()`, `digCap()`, `tmu()`, or `smartVec()` class

With this feature enabled, the SmartRDI verifies whether the label content corresponds to the code in the `RDI_BEGIN()/RDI_END()` block and reports an error when a difference is detected.

 |
 | VEC_EDIT_MODE  | Specify this option to select one of vector edit modes: VECD or VEC_TRANSFER_TASK.

If not specified, VECD is used by default.

 |

By default, SMV_IGNORE_COMMENT = FALSE. If you set SMV_IGNORE_COMMENT = TRUE, all smartVec comments inserted by [comment()](<02.07.13.24.05_comment.md>) will be ignored in pattern generation.

dataMode

 |

The sequence to read and write data of multiple pins. It can be:

1: Read and write the data horizontally, which means reading and writing the data in the order of the first data of all pins, the second data of all pins, and then the rest data for all the pins.

0: Read and write the data vertically, which means reading and writing the data of the first pin, and then the data of second pin and the data of other pins one by one.

You can find more details below the table.

When instructions are used in the protocol template label, you need to specify the cycle offset number to read the data.

 |
 |

writeTemplatePatternName

The pattern used as write template.

The pin(s) to write.

If a pin group name is specified for the parameter, all the pins in the group have the same data to be written to them. If a pin list is specified for the parameter, the address data is written to pins in serial order.

 |
 |

writeAddressVectorNumberLSB

 |

The vector number for the LSB of the address to write.

 |

 |
 |

readVectorsPerRegister

 |

Pattern Tool

Run the MAIN label for the test.

Item

 |

Function

 |
 |

Measure

 |

Use the Measure selection to perform a regular fixture delay measurement on the selected channels.

 |
 |

Measure with dual transmission lines

 |

In some test applications a DUT board is designed such that two pogo pins are connected to one device pin. For example, one pogo pin is used for the drive signal and the other pogo pin is used for the receive signal. This is done to eliminate the "round trip" signal delay. To measure the fixture delay on this type of DUT board, select the channels for measurement, then use the Measure with Dual Transmission Lines selection from the Execute menu. This measurement requires you to place a short device on the DUT board. The short device is a pseudo-device that connects all signal pins to ground.

 |

DPS set ID

 |

This replaces DPS set number in an equation-based environment. It is derived from equation set number and specset number using the following calculation:

`100000 * equation_set_no + 1000 * specset_no + 1`

The purpose of this calculation is to calculate a unique number over 256 - 256 being the highest DPS set number in a non-equation-based environment. This enables equation-based and non-equation-based environments to be mixed.

 |
 |

Equation

 |

A derived variable.

 |
 |

Level equation set

 |

Defines sets of logical test system level resource settings. Logical because they are specified in terms of specs and/or equations which are only evaluated when the equation set is referenced by a level specset - which is where the spec values are assigned. Each level equation set must declare a list of the specs referenced. These must correspond to the specs listed in the level specset.

 |
 |

Level equations

 |

A level setup component where level equation sets are defined. Found after an EQSP LEV,EQN command in a level setup file. Created and modified using a text editor opened from the Timing Setup window.

 |
 |

Level set ID

 |

An equation-based environment. It is derived from equation set number and specset number using the following calculation:

`100000 * equation_set_no + 1000 * specset_no + level_set_no`

The reason for this calculation is to get a unique number over 256 - 256 being the highest level set number in a non-equation-based environment. This enables equation-based and non-equation-based environments to be mixed.

 |
 |

Level specifications

 |

A level setup component where level specsets are defined. Found after an EQSP LEV,SPS command in a level setup file. Created and modified using a text editor or the spec tool opened from the Timing Setup window.

 |
 |

Level Specset

 |

Allocates level sets and one DPS set in hardware by applying spec values to the logical assignments set up in the level equation sets.

 |
 |

Spec

 |

A variable.

 |
 |

Specset ID

 |

Specsets are accessed using a specset ID. This is derived from equation set number and specset number using the following calculation:

`100 * equation_set_no + specset_no`

The purpose for this calculation is to allow blocks of IDs to each equation set. Thus each equation set may be referenced by 100 specsets.

Explanation

GENA <nbr_of_vectors>

 |

Generates vectors for one transaction sequence. This instruction is only visible when the Pattern Debug Tool is in expanded mode.

 |
 |

IDLE <length_of_idle_sequence> <nbr_of_cycles> <time_to_wait>

 |

Waits for the specified number of tester cycles and in addition the specified time (in ns). The specified time is converted into the smallest number n of tester cycles so that n * tester_period ≥ specified_time

The total number of wait cycles can be checked when the Pattern Debug Tool is in expanded mode.

 |
 |

JPPS

 |

Jump to a per pin sequencer subroutine.

 |
 |

MACT <nbr_of_repetitions> <debug_mode>

 |

Indicates the start position of a counted match loop.

<nbr_of_repetitions> specifies the maximum number of unsuccessful repetitions. <debug_mode> specifies whether the match loop is in fact executed as a match loop (DebugOff) or rather as a standard counted loop (DebugOn). For more information see [TRANSACTION_SEQUENCE](<../02.07_Test_Method_Reference/02.07.04.01.256_TRANSACTION_SEQUENCE.md>).

 |
 |

MRPA <nbr_of_vectors>

 |

Indicates the end of the body of a counted match loop.

<nbr_of_vectors> specifies the number of the dummy vectors that are repeated to provide the necessary time for setting the error flag.

 |
 |

WTFM <length_of_idle_sequence> <name_of_synchronization_marker> <port>

 |

Waits until a synchronization point in the simulation port is reached. - UHC4T:

Function

 |

Description

 |
 |

View Waveform Memory

 |

This function allows you to view the waveform stored in waveform memory of arbitrary analog modules.

 |
 |

Signal Information

 |

Displays signal information, such as:

- Mean and standard deviation
- RMS
- Min.value and max.value
- Sample rate

The signal information is displayed on the Signal Analyzer console. Note that when a function is selected, the User Configurable Dialog Box appears allowing you to specify the trace ID.

 |
 |

Spectrum Analysis

 |

Provides several functions, such as: signal- to- noise plus distortion (SND), signal-to- noise ratio (SNR), and total harmonic distortion (THD) for the specified waveform. When a function is selected, the User Configurable Dialog Box appears allowing you to specify the trace ID. Note that the following units are supported for the Spectrum Analysis:

- dB
- dBm
- dBV
- Vp
- Vpp
- Vrms
- Watts

Note that when this function is selected, the Spectrum Analysis Dialog appears allowing you to specify the trace ID, Spectrum Unit, Window function, Carrier Frequency (optional), Carrier Bin (optional). Note that the options Carrier Frequency and Carrier Bin allow you to specify the carrier frequency or bin when SmarTest cannot correctly determine the carrier peak because a peak in the spectrum is higher than the carrier.

 |
 |

Diff. Waveforms

 |

Enables you to calculate the difference between specified waveforms and display it to the selected Data Display Panel. When this function is selected, the User Configurable Dialog Box appears allowing you to specify the trace ID.

 |
 |

Show Histogram

 |

Calculates the histogram of the specified waveform and displays it on a new graph.

 |
 |

Auto Scale

 |

Scales the waveforms in a Data Display Panel to fit into one display.

 |
 |

Clear

 |

Deletes all traces displayed in the selected graph.

 |
 |

Copy

 |

Copies the specified trace of selected graph.

 |
 |

Paste

 |

Pastes the copied trace (using Copy) into selected graph.

 |
 |

Edit Trace

 |

Enables you to edit the data of the specified trace using a default editor. A prerequisite for this is that the environment variable EDITOR is set as in the following example.

`export EDITOR=/usr/X11R6/bin/nedit`

In this example, the Trace Editor is set to be the NEdit tool. You must restart SmarTest in order that this EDITOR variable takes effect.

Specify a color for the cursor in this combo box.

 |

X Track Mode

 |

If the "X Track Mode" is on, the "X Reference Cursor" and "X Measure Cursor" will be synchronized. This means the space between these cursors becomes constant at all times.

Y Track Mode

|

Enable

 |

When this checkbox is selected, the testflow or test suite is executed in a loop according to specifications described below. If it is cleared, the testflow or test suites are executed only once.

 |
 |

Count

 |

The number of loop iterations to be performed.

 |
 |

Loop Indefinitely

 |

If this option is chosen, the testflow or test suite is executed until you give an Abort command, or until the Stop on Fail or Stop on Pass conditions are met.

 |
 |

Stop on Fail

 |

The testflow or test suite is executed until a fail bin is reached that does not have the Overon flag set.

The overall pass/fail result depends on the actual test result, the Set to Fail test suite flag and the Test Level flag.

 |
 |

Stop on Pass

 |

The testflow or test suite is executed until all tests in the sequence have been completed with a pass result.

This is different from Stop on fail in that Stop on fail halts the test when a single fail bin is reached while Stop on pass requires all test suites to pass.

The Hold on Fail or Hold test suite flags still cause the execution to pause. Clicking Continue continues the loop execution. Clicking Abort terminates the loop execution.

 |
 |

Log Loop Number

 |

When this option is enabled, a message is output to the report window at the beginning of each testflow loop iteration, similar to this one:

`Executing Test Flow Loop Iteration: 2`

The current testflow loop number is displayed with the first iteration numbered as 1. No message is output when executing the test suites in a loop.

If multisite testing is also enabled, the loop number is reported only at the beginning of the first tested site.

 |
 |

Pause between loops:

 |

When this option is enabled and a time interval is specified in the ms text box, execution pauses at completion of each loop and waits for the given number of milliseconds before it continues executing the next loop.

You adjust the wait time by changes the numeric input in the ms text box. By default, the value is 0.0 millisecond, that is, no time interval between loops and execution does not pause after each loop.

Always used together with the ms text box to the right of it.

edge_spec

 |

The edge specifier can either be a physical edge (d1 through d8 or r1 through r8), or one of the data parameters D1, D2, C1, C2 (drive parameters) or E1, E2 (receive parameters).

If you specify a physical edge, the dev_cyc_name and the dc_ref parameters must be omitted.

 |
 |

edge_number

 |

In the query reply, this parameter contains the edge that is used as leading or trailing edge.

 |
 |

dev_cyc_name

 |

Specifies the name of a logical device cycle that uses the data parameter given as the edge_spec. It must be defined for all pins in pinlist. If you do not enter a name in this parameter, the first device cycle in the device cycle table is used.

 |
 |

dc_ref

 |

This parameter specifies whether the leading or the trailing edge that is associated with the specified dev_cyc_name and dc_ref parameters is to be returned. The two options are LE (for "leading edge") and TE (for "trailing edge").

The leading edge is always the first edge that is associated with the specified data parameter within the specified device cycle,

The trailing edge is determined differently for drive and receive parameters:

- Drive parameter: The trailing edge is the first drive edge after the leading edge that performs a data or tri-state action.
- Receive parameter: If the action of the leading edge is an edge compare, leading and trailing edge will be identical. If it is the start action of a window compare, then the associated window close edge is the trailing edge.
 |
 |

direction

 |

This parameter can be in or out. If in is selected to define an input edge, then the edge_spec parameter must be D1, D2, C1, or C2. If out is selected to define a receiver edge, then the edge_spec parameter must be E1 or E2. If either in or out is selected along with an edge_spec parameter of 1,2...6, then a check is performed to ensure that the edges of all pins are in the required direction. If no entry is made in this parameter, the measuring edges of the pin in pinlist can have any direction or be unused.

 |
 |

reuse_flag

 |

The reuse flag is returned by the system. A flag is returned only for the device cycle specified in the dev_cyc_name parameter of the EDDC? query, and only if D1, D2, C1, C2, E1, or E2 has been selected as the edge_spec. The reuse flag can be:

- R: The returned edge is used in another device cycle.
- N: The returned edge is not used in another device cycle.
 |
 |

pinlist

 |

The parameters of the EDDC? command are applied to all pins named in this parameter. If more than one pin is used, the names must be separated by a comma.

In a multi-port setup, all pins must belong to the same port of the specification that was entered as the first parameter.

definition_string

The definition string consists of a sequence of items each of which associates a delay with a drive or compare edge. On Pin Scale 800/3600 boards, drive edges are denoted by dn. On Pin Scale 9G boards, there are two kinds of drive edges, which are denoted by fn and sn, respectively; for details see [Defining waveforms for Pin Scale 9G pins](<../02.06_Command_Reference/02.06.06.01.03.02_Defining_waveform_shapes_for_Smart_Scale_pins.md>). You can also use the dn notation for Pin Scale 9G channels, but mixing both notations in one string is not allowed. Receive edges are always denoted by rn.

Unless you employ the pdiv statement for fast pins (see below), all edges which are not explicitly set remain unchanged.

The range of the edge delay is -8000 ns to +24000 ns (or -4 to +12 test system periods) for the Pin Scale 3600/800.

On Pin Scale 800/3600 boards, the restrictions for edge ordering must be observed both in fixed and equation based timing. For example, you cannot assign a greater delay to d1 than to d3 if d1 precedes d3 in a waveform definition. For more information, see [Selecting and ordering edges](<../02.06_Command_Reference/02.06.06.01.03.01.02_Selecting_and_ordering_edges.md>).

Note that with equation based timing, ETDS returns no error message when the edge order restrictions are violated.

If a pin is configured as a fast pin in the context of the specification given by the first parameter, you can specify the period divider at the start of the definition string. If you omit either pdiv or the first edge, only the specified edges are modified. However, with receive edges this is only possible for r1.

The calculated delays are determined for the ith edge by the following formula:

 1st_edge_delay + (i-1) * (period/pdiv)

1st_edge_delay is the delay specified for the first edge (d1 or r1; the generic notation e1 is not allowed for fast pins). If the first edge is not specified in the string, its delay is set to 0. An example for the calculation will be given below.

Note that when both the period divider and a delay for the first edge are present in the definition string, then the delays for all the edges required by the period divider will be overwritten.

When a delay is explicitly specified for one of the edges, this delay overrides the calculated default. There are two formats to specify overrides. You can either define absolute delays or the offsets from the default delays.

Specsets are accessed using a specset ID. This is derived from equation set number and specset number using the following calculation:

orig:
|

abort

 |

if set, it will produce a predefined sequence of events, whereby the post-actions of successively higher levels are executed, one after the other, until the last level is exited.

 |
 |

pause

 |

a special condition that has its own defined section in the application model file (the ON_PAUSE section). If the pause flag/button is set, the actions and dialogs that are defined in the ON_PAUSE section are executed. You then have the choice of quitting or continuing.

 |
 |

reset

 |

is identical to abort, but in addition the tester hardware is reset.

 |
 |

skip

 |

if set, the pre- and post-actions on the level where the skip occurs are executed; all lower levels are skipped.

 |
 |

retest_d

 |

(retest die) can only be set at the device level; it causes the last die tested to be tested once more, and the results to be logged.

 |
 |

check_dev

 |

(check device) can only be set at the device level; it causes the device to be tested without logging of the results (but a summary does appear in the report window)

 |
 |

retest_w

 |

(retest wafer) can be set in the wafer level and the ON_PAUSE section. It results in the last tested wafer being tested once more, and the results being logged.

 |
 |

reference

 |

can be set in the wafer level and in the ON_PAUSE section. If set, the reference wafer will be loaded and tested. However, your own prober driver must be able to support the reference event; this means it must be able to,

1. stop testing of the current wafer

2. remove the current wafer

3. load the reference wafer

4. test the reference wafer

5. remove the reference wafer

6. reload the wafer you had been testing

7. test this wafer again

 |
 |

quit

 |

can be set in all levels. If set, the software moves back up through the levels, executing all post-actions, until it reaches the next dialog - which is then executed.

 |

Aspect

 |

Used settings

 |
 |

`handler_family`

 |

Advantest, the name of the handler family. It must be defined.

 |
 |

`model`

 |

The name of a specific handler model within the handler family.

- R7.2.3 only supports M45 and M48 handler families, including M4871.
- R7.3.2 starts to support DLT handlers.
- R7.3.3 starts to support Yushan handlers.
 |
 |

`driver_message_log`

 |

The location of the driver message log file. The default value is "".

 |
 |

`debug_level`

 |

The debug level of the driver, -1 to 4, or 9. The default value is 1.

 |
 |

`stop_handler_on_smartest_pause`

 |

Stop the handler or not when SmarTest is paused, the default value is no.

 |
 |

`interface_type`

 |

gpib, the handler interface type. It must be defined and has no default value.

 |
 |

`symbolic_interface_name`

 |

hpib, the name of the interface device. It must be defined and has no default value.

 |
 |

`gpib_port`

 |

22, the GPIB port number of the prober or handler.

 |
 |

`handler_site_ids`

 |

The names of the handler sites, which must be defined and has no default value.

 |
 |

`handler_site_mask`

 |

Mask of active handler sites, entries can be 0 or 1, and the default value is [ 1 1 1 ... ].

 |
 |

`smartest_site_to_handler_site_map`

 |

Mapping of SmarTest sites to handler sites, entries are >= 1, the default value is [ 1 2 3 ... ].

 |
 |

`bin_mapping`

 |

Method of SmarTest to handler bin mapping. Supported values are default, mapped-hardbins, or mapped-softbins.

- default

This is the easiest way to specify the device binning. SmarTest's hardbin numbers are used to map SmarTest bins to handler bins in a straight one-to-one mode.

The SmarTest bin with hardbin number 0 is mapped to the first handler bin, the SmarTest bin with hardbin number 1 is mapped to the second handler bin, and so on. There are no further parameters to be set.

- mapped-hardbins

This setting allows you to assign SmarTest bins to handler bins, either individually or in group. The hardbin numbers of the SmarTest bins are used for bin identification.

To use this feature, the parameters handler_bin_ids and hardbin_to_handler_bin_map must be defined.

- mapped-softbins

This setting allows you to assign SmarTest bins to handler bins, either individually or in group. The softbin codes of the SmarTest bins are used for bin identification.

To use this feature, the parameters handler_bin_ids and softbin_to_handler_bin_map must be defined.

See [Configuration Parameters for Binning Management](<02.09.01.03.05.07_Configuration_Parameters_for_Binning_Management.md>) for more bin management information.

 |
 |

`advantest_binning_command_format`

 |

For the Advantest handlers, it defines the binning command format to be used by the driver.

The Advantest handlers support different GPIB command formats for 16-bin and 32-bin configurations.

For the default bin_mapping, the value must be either 16-bin or 32-bin.

For mapped-hardbins and mapped-softbins, the value must match the bin number defined by the handler_bin_ids.

 |
 |

`waiting_for_parts_method`

 |

How to wait for test-start signals on the GPIB port, polling or interrupt. The default value is interrupt.

 |
 |

`srq_mask`

 |

The mask bits of the status byte. The default value is FF.

 |
 |

`thermal_alarm_srq_list`

 |

The thermal alarm SRQ list, It must be defined and has no default value.

 |

Comment

 |

Init:<configuration>

 |

 |

 |
 |

Configuration: <temperature setup> <testset setup> <sitemap setup> <siteselection setup> <bincategory setup>

 |

 |

At startup, these setups will be made and the relevant GPIB commands will be sent to the handler.

 |
 |

temperature setup:

`SETTEMP <value>`

`SETBAND <value>`

`SETSOAK <value>`

 |

`"SettingOK"`

 |

Different temperature setups are made according to the value of configuration parameter temp_control:

off or manual: no temperature setting will be sent to the handler.

ambient: disable the temperature controls.

active, hot or cca: the left temperature setup GPIB commands will be sent to handler.

 |
 |

testset setup: (for MR5800)

`TESTSET <value>,<value>,<value>`

 |

`"SettingOK"`

 |

The three values are Para, Step and Row, representing the configuration of test tray.

Para=32/64/128 (test in parallel),

Step=1/2/4(number of test step),

Row should be set to F (1 1 1 1). `Para*Step` must be equal to 128.

 |
 |

sitemap setup:(for MR5800)

SITEMAP <value>

 |

`"SettingOK"`

 |

 |
 |

siteselection setup:(for MR5800)

`SITESEL <value>`

 |

`"SettingOK"`

 |

The value is determined by the configuration parameter handler_site_mask.

 |

`"SettingOK"`

 |

wait for devices: <SRQ><poll>

Handler sends test start SRQ.

 |
 |

`Poll: FULLSITES?`

Handler returns bit coded site number.

 |

 |

 |

 |

bin devices:

Bin the devices. "n" represents the bin code string for all the sites, like "`xxxxxxxx,xxxxxxxx,xxxxxxxx,xxxxxxxx`". The first character is the Site 32's (16's for MR660) bin code, and the last character is the Site 1's bin code.

default

32 (SmarTest hardbins 0 through 31), bin 0 represents the SmarTest reset bin.

Reprobe mode

 |

Automatic reprobe on a per site mode, if devices fall into SmarTest reprobe bins.

 |
 |

Reprobe bin number

 |

31, represents number sent to handler upon receiving a SmarTest reprobe bin. Must be changed to correct value according to set up of handler. Note that the reprobe mechanism refers to the disconnection and reconnection of the device before a retest is performed.

To disable this setting remove the "handler_reprobe_bin" parameter and set the "automatic_reprobe_mode" to "off"

 |
 |

Temperature parameters

 |

(MT93xx only) Temperature control may be activated by changing the parameter temp_control to "active" and setting the temp_setpoint.

 |
 |

Test start detection

 |

Done by interrupt (SRQ), can be changed to pure polling mode with given polling interval for troubleshooting.

 |
 |

End-of-line terminator

 |

Driver sends CR+LF and EOI on the GPIB bus, cannot be changed through configuration file. Driver expects no special end of line code from handler except EOI.

 |
 |

Polling interval

 |

Preset to 100 ms, only used if waiting for parts is done by polling.

 |

The query results are represented by a ParamList object. It contains the following members:

- BOARD_TYPE: The test board type. It can be CHANNEL_BOARD, DPS_BOARD, CLOCK_BOARD, CONTROL_BOARD.
- SLOT: The pogo block number of the test board.
- PART_NUMBER: The part number of the test board.
- SERIAL_NUMBER: The serial number of the test board.
- VENDOR: The vendor information of the test board.
- VERSION: The version information of the test board.
- REPAIR: How many times the test board has been repaired.
- FPGAREVS: The whole FPGA revisions on a board. The FPGA revision is presented by a hexadecimal number which begins with "0x". The whole FPGA revisons string may have a maximum of 8 FPGA revisions separated by ",".
- HW_TYPE: The hardware type.

For channel board, it can be C, CE, or P.

For DPS board, it can be DCS-UHC4T or DCS-DPS128.

- MAX_SPEED: (Only for channel board) The maximal speed of the board.
- MODULE_ID_LIST: The ID list for the test modules in the board. This is not available for RF board.
- PHY_LOCATION: The physical location of the board. It is in the format TCSS:

T: The test head number. It is always 1 for 93000.

C: The card cage number. It can be an integer from 1 to 8.

SS: The slot number in the card cage. It can be a two-digit interger from 00 to 14.

Event

 |

BLC API

 |

Current application model behaviors

 |
 |

Reprobe

 |

SetReprobeAction()

 |

Once the device is binned to a reprobe bin, the testflow execution engine FTEST will call the CI function which is registered by the application model keyword REPROBE_ACTION.

 |
 |

Pause

 |

IsPaused()

 |

Pop up a dialog and wait for the operator's intervention if a dialog is specified in the PAUSE section; if no dialog is specified, the test will also be paused until the operator pushed the Pause button again.

 |
 |

Abort

 |

IsInterrupted()

 |

Abort the execution of the test program.

 |
 |

Reset

 |

IsInterrupted()

 |

Abort the execution of the test program.

 |
 |

Level End

 |

IsLotDone()

IsCassetteDone()

IsWaferDone()

IsDeviceDone()

 |

The current generic Prober/Handler driver sets a flag when the driver thinks the test of a lot, wafer, cassette or device level is finished. Application model will exit the current level if this production flag is set.

 |
 |

Retest Device

 |

SetSpecialBLCTestEnv()

 |

Set the production flag to retest the device and then give the control to the testflow execution engine (FTEST) and the handler driver. FTEST will update the bin counting information based on the flag. The prober/handler driver will not get new devices since it is in a retest device cycle.

 |
 |

Check Device

 |

SetSpecialBLCTestEnv()

 |

Set the flag to check the device and then give the control to the testflow execution engine (FTEST) and the prober/handler driver. FTEST will update the bin counting information based on the flag. The handler driver will not get new devices since it is in a check device cycle.

 |
 |

Retest Wafer

 |

SetSpecialBLCTestEnv()

 |

Set the production flag to retest the wafer, jump out the die test level loop, and then restart the test of the wafer. The prober will keep the current wafer.

 |
 |

Reference Wafer

 |

SetSpecialBLCTestEnv()

 |

Set the production flag to reference a wafer, jump out the die test level loop, and then restart the test of the wafer. The prober will load the reference wafer.

 |

- SITE_SETUP_FOR_SITES: The setup status for all the sites. The format of this parameter looks like "I X I I I X X I". Each character in the string is corresponding to the site ID in the site ID list. "I" means the site is inserted and "X" means there is no device on the corresponding site.
- PACKAGE_ID_FOR_SITES: The package ID list for all the sites. The format of this parameter looks like "p1 p2 p3 p4 p5 p6 p7 p8". This means the package ID for site "1" is "p1" and so forth. If the corresponding site is not inserted, then the package ID for that site is "-1".
- DIE_X_FOR_SITES: The X coordinate list for all the sites. The format of this parameter looks like "1 2 3 1 2 3 1 2".
- DIE_Y_FOR_SITES: The Y coordinate list for all the sites. The format of this parameter looks like "1 1 1 2 2 2 3 3".

<backup?> (number) specifies whether STPM generates a backup copy of each modified file:

- 0: No backups are generated.
- 1: Backups are generated.

<test_group> (string) is the testflow group in which the test suite is generated.

If this parameter is not specified, the test suite is generated at the root of the MTP, at the end of the testflow.

 |
 |

test

 |

<test> is the name for the added test in the MTP.

If this parameter is omitted, the name is added to the MTP with the same name that it has in the STP.

If there is already a test with the same name in the MTP, the test from the STP is not added and an error is generated. (This applies in both cases, whether you have specified a name using the test parameter or whether the default name is used.)

position

 |

<position> (string) is the position within a test group where the new test is inserted.

The following values are available:

- optimal: STPM inserts the test in a position in the testflow group that requires the least amount of level and timing reloads during execution.
- first: The test suite is inserted as the first test in the testflow group.
- last: The test suite is inserted as the last in the testflow group.
- after:<test_name>: The test suite is inserted immediately after the test suite with the name <test_name> in the testflow group.
- before:<test_name>: The test suite is inserted immediately before the test suite with the name <test_name> in the testflow group.

If this parameter is omitted, optimal is used.

If the test_group parameter (see above) is omitted, the position parameter is ignored.

 |
 |

tim_reuse

 |

<timing_reuse> (string) is the way in which timing settings in the MTP are to be reused for the added test:

- auto: STPM tries to reuse an existing timing, merging the timing from the new test with it. If this is not possible, a new timing is created.
- test:<test-name>: The timing from the existing test suite with the name <test-name> is used for the added test.
- <primary-keys>: You can explicitly specify the timing to use. How to do this differs for single-port and multiport tests:

  - Single-port timing: Specify the timing as a combination of indexes, separated by periods: <eqnset-index>`.`<timset-index>`.`<specset-index>
  - Multiport timing: Specify the name of the multiport specification to use.

- none: STPM will not try to reuse any timing. Instead, it always creates new timing for the added test.

If this parameter is omitted, none is used.

 |
 |

lev_reuse

 |

<level_reuse> (string) is the way in which level settings in the MTP are to be reused for the added test:

- auto: STPM tries to reuse existing levels, merging the levels from the new test with hem. If this is not possible, new levels are created.
- test:<test-name>: The levels from the existing test suite with the name <test-name> are used for the added test.
- <primary-keys>: You can explicitly specify the levels to use as a combination of indexes, separated by periods:

<eqnset-index>`.`<levelset-index>`.`<specset-index>

- none: STPM will not try to reuse any levels. Instead, it always creates new levels for the added test.

If this parameter is omitted, none is used.

 |
 |

pat_reuse

 |

<pattern_reuse> (string) is the way in which patterns in the MTP are to be reused for the added test:

- test:<test-name>: The patterns from the existing test suite with the name <test-name> are used for the added test.
- <pattern-label>: You can explicitly specify the patterns to use by providing the name of the pattern label.
- none: STPM will not try to reuse any patterns. Instead, it always creates new patterns for the added test.

If this parameter is omitted, none is used.

 |
 |

reuse_scope

 |

<scope> (string or list of strings) are the testflow groups that STPM is to analyze for purposes of merging or reusing primaries. STPM will ignore primaries from other testflow groups.

The scope can be:

- `"*all*"` to tell STPM to consider all groups
- A comma-separated list of testflow groups, enclosed in square brackets

If this parameter is not specified, the default is for STPM to consider the test suites in the testflow group specified in the test_group parameter (see above).

If test_group is not specified either, all groups are considered.

 |
 |

pat_dir

 |

<path> (string) is the path of the directory where STPM is to store patterns that it copies from the STP to the device directory.

The path is relative to the vectors subdirectory of the device directory.

If this parameter is omitted, patterns is used. (That is, the patterns are copied to the vectors/patterns/ subdirectory of the device directory.)

test_flags

<test_flags> (list of strings) is a list of test suite flags that are enabled for the imported test. The list must be enclosed in square brackets.

Include in the list each test suite flag you want to be enabled for the test in the MTP, enclosed in quotes and separated by commas.

- bypass
- fail_per_label
- ffc_enable
- ffc_scan_enable
- ffv_enable
- frg_enable
- frg_single_shot
- hold
- hold_on_fail
- mx_waves_enable
- output_on_fail
- output_on_pass
- per_pin_on_fail
- per_pin_on_pass
- set_pass
- set_fail
- value_on_fail
- value_on_pass

For example: `test_flags = ['hold_on_fail','per_pin_on_fail']`

If this parameter is omitted, no flags are enabled for the test.

 |
 |

test_method

 |

<method> (string) is the class of the test method of the test being added (for example, "ac_tml.AcTest.FunctionalTest").

If this parameter is omitted, the test is added to the MTP with the same type that it has in the STP.

 |
 |

test_params

 |

<params> (list of name/value pairs) is a list of parameter values with which to call the test method.

This is a list of name/value pairs that are separated by commas; the entire list is wrapped in curly braces: {<name>':'<value>',...}

Each name and value is a string, both are separated by a colon:

- <name> is the name of a parameter that is known to the test method.
- <value> is the value that is passed into this parameter when the test method is called.

For example: `test_params = {'param1':'0','my_param':'CLK'}`

This is an optional parameter. If it is omitted, no parameters are passed to the test method.

 |
 |

sbin_num

 |

<sbin_num> (string) is the software bin ID of the bin associated with the added test.

To be compatible with the SmarTest Data Formatter, the number must be between 0 and 32767.

This is an optional parameter; if hbin_num (see below) is specified, it is required. If it is omitted, a "Run" node without any associated bin is inserted in the test flow.

 |
 |

sbin_label

 |

<description> (string) is a short text describing the purpose of the software bin. It is intended for human readers.

This is an optional parameter. If it is omitted, the bin remains unlabeled.

 |
 |

hbin_num

 |

<hbin_num> (number) is the ID of the hardware bin connected to the software bin you are defining.

This is an optional parameter. If sbin_num (see above) is not specified, the hbin_num parameter cannot be specified.

 |
 |

hbin_label

 |

<hbin_label> (string) is a short text describing the purpose of the hardware bin. It is intended for human readers.

This is an optional parameter. If it is omitted, the bin remains unlabeled.

 |
 |

pre_proc

 |

<pre_proc> is a script that is executed before this command.

The syntax of the parameter value is described in [Preprocessing and postprocessing scripts](<02.09.02.03.03_Preprocessing_and_postprocessing_scripts.md>).

This is an optional parameter.

 |
 |

post_proc

 |

<post_proc> is a script that is executed after this command.

The syntax of the parameter value is described in [Preprocessing and postprocessing scripts](<02.09.02.03.03_Preprocessing_and_postprocessing_scripts.md>).

This is an optional parameter.

 |

 |

If this parameter is set to -1, no CCT integration is possible.

This parameter is required if the CCT mode is used; otherwise it is optional. The default is -1.

 |
 |

apply_prefix_on_specs_and_equations

 |

Default = 1.

<apply_prefix_flag> (integer) specifies whether STPM MCM applies the prefix defined for an STP (see [STP table](<02.09.03.04.01_STP_table.md>) for details) to the specs and equation variables it imports from that STP to the MTP:

- 0: The names of specs and equation variables copied from the STP are not changed; the prefixes are ignored.
- 1: When a spec or equation variable is imported from the STP to the MTP, the prefix defined for the STP is added to its name.

Note that the application of prefixes to pin configuration objects is controlled individually for each STP through the Apply Prefix On Pin Config column in the [STP table](<02.09.03.04.01_STP_table.md>).

This parameter is optional. The default is 1.

 |

The available settings depend on the specified ate_target.

For '93000SS', you can specify:

- 'PS1600'

 |

ate_config_msdps

 |

A list with the channel numbers of the DSP modules.

<module> (integer or range) is one module or a range of modules:

- One module: Specify the number of the module, for example, 3.
- Range of modules: Specify the first and last module in the range, separated by a dash. For example, 2-4.

You can specify multiple modules or module ranges; separate them with commas. The list of modules (whether you specify one or more) must be enclosed in curly brackets.

This is an optional parameter. If it is omitted, STPM MCM determines the channel mode automatically by assigning mode 8 to every module that has a channel number greater than four and mode 4 to all other modules.

stp_missing_primaries

 |

What STPM MCM is to do when an STP uses missing primaries.

<behavior> can be any of these:

- 'error': An error is generated and the creation of the MTP is stopped.
- 'warning': A warning is generated but the MTP is created. The test suite from the STP is integrated without change; STPM MCM leaves the references to the missing primaries unchanged.
- 'bypass': STPM behaves differently depending on whether the test suite is bypassed:

If the test suite is bypassed, STPM behaves as for 'warning'.

If the test suite is not bypassed, STPM behaves as for 'error'.

STPM considers a test suite bypassed if the local bypass flag of the test suite is set, if the bypass flag is set for it in the [MTPT test flag table](<02.09.03.04.11_Test_flag_table.md>), or if it is part of a group for which the bypass flag has been set.

This is an optional parameter. If it is not specified, 'bypass' is used.

-system

   | |

 |

 |

n/a

 |

- If 0, no timeout occurred.

- If 0, the test was not executed.

- If 0, the test was not aborted.
- If 1, the test was aborted. | | | | | Bit 6:

- If 0, there is a pass/fail flag
- If 1, the test was completed. | | | | | Bit 7:

- If 0, the test passed.

First byte is unsigned count of bytes to follow

Maximum 255 bytes

First byte is unsigned count of bytes to follow

Maximum 255 bytes

- 0: The tester does not perform dual side comparison
- 1: Z is mapped to L
- 2: Z is mapped to H
- 3: Z is mapped to Z )If Z is expected, it is mapped to the mid-level between L and H.)
- 4: Z is mapped to X | | | FMU_FLG | The statuses of the failure map and the mask map | Variable-length bit-encoded field | | | | | Bits 0 and 1:

- 00: No mask map is present, no pin is globally masked.
- 01: No mask map (MASK_MAP) present, use previous mask map definition.

- 11: Not used. | | | | | Bits 2 and 3:

- 00: No information on the buffer status is present or all tests have passed.

0: the number of failures could not be determined or there were no failures | | | TOTL_CNT | The total number of failures logged during the test.

Supported values: 1, 2 | | | CHN_SIZE | The size in bytes of the CHN_NUM array members | One-byte unsigned integer

Supported values: 1, 2, 4 | | | U1_SIZE | The size in bytes of the USR1 array members | One-byte unsigned integer

Supported values: 1, 2, 4, 8 | | | U2_SIZE | The size in bytes of the USR2 array members | One-byte unsigned integer

Supported values: 1, 2, 4, 8 | | | U3_SIZE | The size in bytes of the USR3 array members | One-byte unsigned integer

Supported values: 1, 2, 4, 8 | | | UTX_SIZE | The size in characters of the USER_TXT array members | One-byte unsigned integer

A value from 1 to 255 | | | CAP_BGN | Offset added to the BIT_POS value for failures logged in the PAT_NUM and BIT_POS fields. | Two-byte unsigned integer

This number can be an arbitrary number, which must be bigger than the maximum scan chain pattern length.

Each value is a two-byte unsigned integer

The first array element (element 0) is reserved for indicating all pins or default pins. | | | LIM_SPEC | An array of fail logging limits for the pins listed in LIM_INDX | Array with the dimension LIM_CNT

Each entry has the form `=`.

Index between 1 and 32767

Each value is a fixed-length unsigned integer with the length CYC_SIZE | | | PMR_CNT | The number of elements in the PMR_INDX array | Two-byte unsigned integer

|

PTR field name

 |

Field description

 |

Value

 |

93000 data source

 |
 |

TEST_NUM

 |

- Test number
 |

- Four-byte unsigned integer
- In multi-port testing, a single pattern port or a specified combination of pattern ports in a test suite is treated as a test.
- Valid test number is required for reliable analysis.
 |

- EDL Event:

TestSuiteStartEventType

Test

- EDL Attribute:

TestIdAttrType

 |
 |

HEAD_NUM

 |

- Test head number
 |

- One-byte unsigned integer
- Value = 1

If the ATR and GDR indicate that there are more than 255 sites in the test, HEAD_NUM is the number of the site divided by 256. For example, in a record for site 384, HEAD_NUM would be 2.

 |

- For tests with up to 255 sites: hard-coded value

For tests with more than 255 sites: derived from SiteID

 |
 |

SITE_NUM

 |

- Test site number
 |

- One-byte unsigned integer

If the ATR and GDR indicate that there are more than 255 sites in the test, SITE_NUM is the number of the site modulo 256. For example, in a record for site 600, SITE_NUM would be 88.

 |

- EDL Event:

TestFlowStartEventType

- EDL Attribute:

SiteIdAttrType

 |
 |

TEST_FLG

 |

- Test flags
 |

- Variable length bit-encoded field
 |

 |
 |

 |

(fail, alarm, etc.)

 |

Bit 0:

0 = No alarm has been logged.

1 = An alarm has been logged.

   | |
 |

 |

 |

Bit 1:

Reserved. Always 0.

 |

- Hard-coded value
 |
 |

 |

 |

Bit 2:

0 = Test is reliable. Default.

1 = Test is unreliable

 |

- EDL Event:

TestEventType

- EDL Attribute:

ValueResultAttrType

MeasuredRangeAttrType

 |
 |

 |

 |

Bit 3:

0 = No timeout

 |

- Hard-coded value
 |
 |

 |

 |

Bit 4:

0 = Test suite executed

 |

- Hard-coded value
 |
 |

 |

 |

Bit 5:

0 = No abort. Always 0.

 |

- Hard-coded value
 |
 |

 |

 |

Bit 6:

0 = Test suite bypassed, Bit 7 not valid. Default.

1 = Test suite not bypassed, and Bit 7 is valid.

 |

- EDL Event:

TestEventType

- EDL Attribute:

PassFailResultAttrType

 |
 |

 |

 |

Bit 7:

0 = Test passed

1 = Test failed

 |

- EDL Event:

TestEventType

- EDL Attribute:

PassFailResultAttrType

 |
 |

PARM_FLG

 |

- Parametric test flags
 |

- Variable length bit-encoded field
 |

 |
 |

 |

(drift, etc.)

 |

Bit 0:

0 = No scale error.

 |

- Hard-coded value
 |
 |

 |

 |

Bit 1:

0 = No drift error.

 |

- Hard-coded value
 |
 |

 |

 |

Bit 2:

0 = No oscillation detected.

 |

- Hard-coded value
 |
 |

 |

 |

Bit 3:

0 = Measured value not higher than the high test limit.

1 = Measured value higher than high test limit

 |

- EDL Event:

TestEventType

- EDL Attribute:

ValueResultAttrType

MeasuredRangeAttrType

-  This bit is set if at least one measured value is greater than the high limit.
 |
 |

 |

 |

Bit 4:

0 = Measured value not lower than low test limit.

1 = Measured value lower than low test limit

 |

- EDL Event:

TestEventType

- EDL Attribute:

ValueResultAttrType

MeasuredRangeAttrType

- This bit is set if at least one measured value is less than the low limit.
 |
 |

 |

 |

Bit 5:

0 = Test failed, or passed standard limits

 |

- Hard-coded value
 |
 |

 |

 |

Bit 6:

0 = Failed because test result = low limit.

1 = Passed because test result = low limit

 |

- EDL Event:

TestEventType

- EDL Attribute:

PassRangeAttrType

 |
 |

 |

 |

Bit 7:

0 = Failed because test result = high test limit

1 = Passed because test result = high test limit.

 |

- EDL Event:

TestEventType

- EDL Attribute:

PassRangeAttrType

 |
 |

RESULT

 |

- Test result
 |

- Four-byte floating point number
- The RESULT field is considered valid only if TEST_FLG bits 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 and PARM_FLG bits 0, 1, and 2 are all set to 0.
- If any of these bits are set to 1, then the RESULT field is invalid.
 |

- EDL Event:

TestEventType

- EDL Attribute:

TestValueResult -> Value

MeasuredRange -> MinValue

 |
 |

TEST_TXT

 |

- Test description text or label
 |

- Variable length character string
- First byte is unsigned count of bytes to follow
- Maximum 255 bytes
- Length byte = 0 if invalid or missing data
- For multi_port testing, contains the string <test suite name>@<pattern port name>.
- The test text contains: "Test suite name: test name#test comment" for MPR's and FTR's. Where '#' is the separator which can be configured in the config file. The comment is logged from the test method api and is optional.
- It contains "Test suite name: test name#pin name#test comment" for PTR's if there is a pin name associated with the PTR. Where '#' is the separator which can be configured in the config file. The comment is logged from the test method api and is optional.
 |

- EDL Event:

TestSuiteEndEventType

TestEventType

User Procedure

- EDL Attribute:

TestSuiteNameAttrType

TestSuiteNameAttrType + port

 |
 |

ALARM_ID

- Name of alarm

- Variable length character string
- First byte is unsigned count of bytes to follow
- Maximum 255 bytes
- Length byte = 0 if invalid or missing data
- If the alarm flag (bit 0 of TEST_FLG) is set, this field can contain the name or ID of the alarms that were triggered.
- Alarm names are tester-dependent.
 |

- Hard-coded value

 |

OPT_FLAG

 |

- Optional data flag
 |

- Variable length bit-encoded field
 |

 |
 |

 |

- The OPT_FLAG field may be omitted if it is the last field in the record
 |

Bit 0:

0 = RES_SCAL value is valid. Always 0.

 |

- Hard-coded value
 |
 |

 |

 |

Bit 1:

Reserved, must be 1.

 |

- Hard-coded value
 |
 |

 |

 |

Bit 2:

1 = No low specification limit. Always 1.

 |

- Hard-coded value
 |
 |

 |

 |

- 12 = Bit encoded data (first two bytes of string are length in bits)
- 13 = Unsigned integer data stored in 4 bits of a byte (nibble)

The GDR is a catch-all data type for all kinds information that does not fit into any of the other record types.

 |
 |

-S

 |

Both the ASCII vector table and the scan instance data are translated. In this case the ASCII interface creates a rudimentary MAIN pattern from which the subroutine is called. If the ASCII vector file contains m blocks of SCAN_DATA sections, this MAIN pattern will repeat the call m times (using the RPTJ instruction).

 |
 |

-SI

 |

Only the SCAN_DATA sections are translated. In this case only the download commands for the scan vectors are created, but no sequencer program and no download commands for the parallel vectors.

 |
 |

 |

Only the ASCII vector table is translated. A sequencer program and download commands for the parallel vectors are created, but no commands for the scan vectors. The numerical value <st_w> of the -u parameter defines the so called stepwidth. The stepwidth is the amount by which the vector translation increments the minor instance offsets of successive SCAN instructions (if they use the same template) within the subroutine.

 |

Log file. Use this option to specify a name and location for the log file. If you Do not give this option, the log file will be created with the primary name given in -o.

 |

b2a interactive translation mode.

-It is b2a timing translation

-Iv is b2a vector translation.

If no -I is given, b2a translation mode is batch mode.

 |
 |

-h

 |

help

 |
 |

-v

 |

b2a tool version information

 |
 |

-F (d|s[n]|w|m|b|c|S|v[n])

 |

d: Process duplicate binary waveforms

 |
 |

 |

s[n]: Insert a space after every n state characters in the ASCII vector file

 |
 |

 |

w: Process every waveform of the wavetable. By default only those waveforms are processed that are included in the #USED WAVEFORMS lines of the respective timing set. This flag must be set if the timing was generated by the ASCII Interface, but additional waveforms were created manually.

 |
 |

 |

v[n]: This option has the following effects in the ASCII vector file:

- Insert CR after n pins in the FORMAT statement
- Add line numbers as comments after the ASCII vectors
- Insert a space after every n state characters in every vector line.
 |
 |

 |

m: Support mixed ASCII dvc's for x-mode factors > 1.

 |
 |

 |

b: This option tells b2a to recover the original ASCII device cycle names from the binary comments (BCMT command) in the binary vector file. aiv generates these comments by default, but they can be suppressed. In this case, b2a will issue an error message.

If both b and c are specified, b prevails.

 |
 |

 |

c: This option tells b2a to use the ASCII device cycle names and state characters of the timing map file, as specified in the configuration file (*.bcf), for the timing retranslation.

This is another option to recover the original ASCII names, and in addition also the original state characters.

If both b and c are specified, b prevails.

 |
 |

 |

S: This option tells b2a to use the selectors and state characters of the state mapping tables, as defined in the wavetable, for the timing retranslation. It is based on the fact that when ait creates state mapping tables, it takes the original ASCII device cycle names as the selectors of these tables, and also uses the state characters of the ASCII timing file for them.

This is a third option to recover the original ASCII names and state characters. Note that this option allows you to reconstruct ASCII dvc's that have been merged into one timing set by ait.

For more information on the state mapping tables see [Representing a pattern in device orientation](<../02.06_Command_Reference/02.06.06.01.03.05_Representing_a_pattern_in_device_orientation.md>) and [ait command line parameters](<02.11.02.02.08.01_ait_command_line_parameters.md>).

 |
 |

-d n

 |

Defines the debug level of b2a. n can take the values 1 through 5. These values have the following meanings:

1: Execution details on the macro level

2: Processing status of implicitly given files

3: Information on creation and update of internal database

4: Information about duplicate binary timing or vector data

5: Detailed messages about tool execution

Specifies a vector setup file. To be used only for pattern conversion with the STATEMAP section. See [STATEMAP section and pattern conversion](<02.11.02.04.01.01_STATEMAP_section_and_pattern_conversion.md>).

 |
 |

-P

 |

Selects a pattern in the vector setup file specified with -V. To be used only for pattern conversion with the STATEMAP section. See [STATEMAP section and pattern conversion](<02.11.02.04.01.01_STATEMAP_section_and_pattern_conversion.md>).

 |
 |

-w

Selects a wavetable in the timing setup file specified with -t. To be used only for pattern conversion with the STATEMAP section. See [STATEMAP section and pattern conversion](<02.11.02.04.01.01_STATEMAP_section_and_pattern_conversion.md>).

word

The contents of a memory address. The V93000 test system can define data words up to 512 bits in word width.

device address

 |
 |

logical address

physical address

orig:
|

Name

 |

Comment

 |
 |

TrainingAlgorithm

 |

The training mode for the training:

- FullTraining: Full training searches for both edges of the data eye and calculates the center of the eye from these edges. Any values specified in the PinOffsets parameter added to the position of the first edge to find the starting value for searching for the second edge.
- FastTraining: Fast training searches only for the first edge of an eye. The center of the eye is calculated by adding the PinOffsets value to the position of this edge.
- EmbeddedTraining: Embedded training means using the training logic embedded in HSM3G and HSM6800 cards. This training logic is similar to the one [used by SmarTest](<../02.06_Command_Reference/02.06.09.01.02_Using_embedded_timing_and_level_search_on_a_Smart_Scale_system.md>).

Default value: FullTraining

 |
 |

Address Pin Group

 |

<list of pin groups>. List of setup pin groups, separated by semicolons. Each group consists of one or more pins separated by commas. For example: `A0_Pin; A1_Pin`.

Address pins can be shared pins. However, this test method does not support mixing shared and non-shared pins. In other words, either all pins must be shared or all pins must be non-shared.

The default for this parameter is specified in the [GDDR5 training configuration file](<02.12.02.05.06.03.01_GDDR5_training_configuration_file.md>).

 |
 |

- Yes (Embedded): Centering is done in the test head card. The method used is similar to the one the SmarTest [EyeFinder](<02.12.02.05.06.04_EyeFinder.md>) uses.

The default for this parameter is specified in the [GDDR5 training configuration file](<02.12.02.05.06.03.01_GDDR5_training_configuration_file.md>). | | SweepType | Absolute or Relative. Which values to use for the sweep:

- Absolute: The sweep begins at SweepStart and ends at SweepStop.
- Relative: The sweep begins at (SweepStart + current value of SweepSpecVars) and ends at (SweepStop + current value of SweepSpecVars).

Default value: Absolute |

Name

 |

Comment

 |
 |

TrainingAlgorithm

 |

SpecTraining or EmbeddedTraining

SpecTraining performs the search for the on the test controller workstation as a parallel spec search.

EmbeddedTraining performs the search in the test processor on the test head card.

 |
 |

SourceSyncPinGroups

 |

Pin group. List of source synchronous pin groups (clock domains), separated by a semicolon. Each group must contain one clock output pin and at least one data output pin.

Example:

4 groups: RDQS0o, DQ0o, DQ1o; RDQS1o, DQ15o; RDQS2o, DQ_Bus2;ssgroup3

The sequence of the pins must match the sequence of the variables.

 |
 |

SweepSpecVars

 |

Spec name. The timing specification variables that are to be used for sweeping the specified source synchronous pin groups, separated by semicolons. Variable names can be identical for different source synchronous pin groups. The number of source synchronous pin groups and the number of timing specification variables need to be the same. The sequence of the specification variables must match the sequence of the pins in the field SourceSyncPinGroups.

Syntax:

For single-port testing:

`{spec_name_0}; {spec_name_1}; ...; {spec_name_n-1}`

spec_name_0, spec_name_1, ... , spec_name_n-1 are names of specification variables.

For multi-port testing:

`{spec_name_0@port_0}; {spec_name_1@port_1}; ...; {spec_name_n-1@port_n-1}`

 |
 |

SweepStart

 |

Number. The starting value for the sweep. The range between SweepStart and SweepStop is swept first using a linear search and then a binary search. The unit is nanoseconds.

 |
 |

SweepStop

 |

Number. The ending value for the sweep. The unit is nanoseconds.

 |
 |

MinOpenEye

 |

Number. The step size of the linear search, specified in nanoseconds. For the sweep to deliver useful results, this must be considerably smaller than the expected minimum eye open time. The unit is nanoseconds.

 |
 |

AlignAccuracy

 |

Number. The resolution (end criterion) of the binary search, specified in nanoseconds.

 |
 |

PrintEye

 |

Yes or No. If Yes output is printed to the report window.

 |
 |

EdgeCentering

 |

Yes or No. If Yes, the edge center timing data in the sweep spec var is used for further measurements in the later test suite.

 |

Parameter

 |

Values and Description

 |
 |

algorithm_lib

 |

The path and file name of the library compiled from the analysis algorithm.

The value can be an absolute path or a relative path from the mts/ra/algorithm/sh_lib/ directory in the current device directory.

See the "Specifying library names" section below this table for details.

 |
 |

algorithm_parameter

 |

A string containing the parameters that are passed to the algorithm.

The number, type, and semantics of these parameters depend on the chosen algorithm. For the default Successive algorithm, they are described in [Parameters of the Successive algorithm](<02.12.02.07.03.02.01_Parameters_of_the_Successive_algorithm.md>).

 |
 |

environment_info

 |

A comma-separated list of environment information:

- Lot ID
- Cassette ID
- Wafer ID
- x-coordinate of the die
- y-coordinate of the die

You can omit individual items by specifying a space for them.

In XML, no quotes around the string are required, but in the .rcs file, it must be enclosed in quotes.

This parameter is optional.

 |
 |

result_root_path

 |

The path under which the result files of the redundancy analysis are stored. (Some files may be stored in subfolders of this directory.)

If this value is not specified, the default <device directory>/mts/ra/result is used.

This parameter is optional.

 |
 |

algorithm_control

 |

The path of the algorithm control file to be used.

This parameter is required only if the algorithm uses a control file. The control file for the default successive algorithm is described in [Control file for the Successive algorithm](<02.12.02.07.03.02.02_Control_file_for_the_Successive_algorithm.md>).

The value can be an absolute path or a relative path from the mts/ra/control_options/ directory in the current device directory.

 |
 |

DUT_rep

 |

The path of the DUT representation shared library to be used.

The DUT representation file for the default successive algorithm is described in [DUT representation file](<02.12.02.07.03.02.03_DUT_representation_file.md>). This file is required for the Successive algorithms and all other algorithms based on the RA algorithm template.

If you write your own algorithm, you may write it in such a way as not to use the DUT representation file, but we do not recommend or support this.

The value can be an absolute path or a relative path from the mts/ra/device_rep/sh_lib/ directory in the current device directory.

See the "Specifying library names" section below this table for details.

This parameter is optional for legacy algorithms.

 |
 |

map_converter

 |

The path of the map converter shared library to be used.

Note that the shared library must implement certain required functions: get_ra_layout and phys_to_layout if the map converter has the type RA_LAYOUT_BASED and get_map_size and phys_to_map if the type is TOPO_MAP_BASED. See [Setting up address scrambling](<02.12.02.05.03_Setting_up_address_scrambling.md>) for more information.

The value can be an absolute path or a relative path from the mts/ra/bitmap/converters/bin/ directory in the current device directory.

See the "Specifying library names" section below this table for details.

If you write your own algorithm, you may write it in such a way as not to use the DUT representation file, but we do not recommend or support this.

 |
 |

ra_counting_enabling

 |

When the failing cell counts generated during the tests are to be summed up by the redundancy analysis algorithm:

- Disable: No summing is performed.
- Enable_on_concurrent_mode: The failed cells are summed after each bit fail map.

This parameter is used only in offline mode, not in online mode.

The default value is Enable_on_concurrent_mode.

 |
 |

ra_algorithm_enabling

 |

When the redundancy analysis algorithm is to be executed:

- Disable: The algorithm is not executed.
- Enable_on_concurrent_mode: The algorithm is executed after each bit fail map.

This parameter is used only in offline mode, not in online mode.

The default value is Disable.

 |
 |

ra_counting_results_leverage

 |

Whether to use the counting results in the execution of the redundancy analysis algorithm:

- YES: The counting results are used. This requires that RA_counting is enabled, that RA_algorithm is enabled, and that the redundancy analysis algorithm supports using the counting results in its analysis.

Note that any combination of concurrent and delayed enabling for counting and algorithm is supported. However, when you specify delayed counting and concurrent execution of the algorithm, the algorithm cannot leverage the counting results.

- NO: The redundancy analysis algorithm does not use the counting results.

This parameter is optional.

The default value is YES.

 |
 |

mapconv_type

 |

The type of the specified map converter:

RA_LAYOUT_BASED: The map converter provides the algorithm that is based on RA layout information, that is, tuples of data bit group, segment, column, and row. The successive algorithm expects this kind of input.

TOPO_ADDR_BASED: The map converter provides the algorithm with input based on topological addresses.

 |
 |

device_path

 |

The path of the device directory of the device to be analyzed.

This parameter is evaluated only in offline mode.

 |
 |

test_name

 |

The name of the test.

In principal, you can use any string here, but we recommend using the name from the test that has been used to create the bitmap file being.

This parameter applies only to offline analysis.

 |
 |

algorithm_timeout

 |

The timeout of the redundancy analysis, in seconds. If the timeout is exceeded, the analysis is considered to have failed and no solution output is created.

A timeout value of -1 or 0 indicates that there is no timeout.

This parameter is optional for online redundancy analysis and required for offline analysis.

 |
 |

faildata_file

 |

The data file containing the fail data that are the input for the redundancy analysis in offline mode.

You can specify a bit fail map (.bfd), a [BFD list file](<02.12.02.07.03.01.05_Bit_fail_map_list_file.md>) (.bfdl), or a physical address-based bit list file (.pabl).

The value can be an absolute path or a relative path from the mts/bitmap/bitmap_data/ directory in the current device directory.

 |

dg

 |

`dg(`i`) = (`begin`, `end`)`

 |

Specify data bit groups: Data bit group i includes all data bits from begin to end.

begin: The data bit with which the group starts.

end: The data bit with which the group ends.

For example: `dg(0) = (1,8)` - Data group 0 includes all bits from 1 through 8.

Currently, only one data bit group - dg(0) - is supported.

 |
 |

sg

 |

`sg(`i`) = (`group`,`x-origin`, `y-origin`,`numrows`, `numcols`)`

 |

Specify segment properties: Segment i belongs to data group group, its origin coordinates are x-origin,y-origin, and it has numrows rows and numcols columns.

group: The data bit group to which the segment belongs

x-origin: The x coordinate of the segment's origin

y-origin: The y coordinate of the segment's origin

numrows: The number of spare rows in the segment

numcols: The number of spare columns in the segment

For example: s`g(2) = (1,0,7,16,8)` - Segment 2 belongs to data group 1; it begins at 0,7; and it has 16 rows and 8 columns.

 |
 |

sra_col

 |

`sra_col(`i`) = (`group`, `spareColNum`, `spareColID`)`

 |

Assign spare columns to segments: Spare column spareColID is assigned to segment i and data bit group group as the spare number spareColNum.

group: The data bit group to which the column belongs

spareColNum: The index of the assigned spare column within the segment' spare columns. This can be a loop.

spareColID: The ID of the spare column being assigned

For example: `sra_col(1) = (3,0,5)` - For segment 1 and data group 3, the spare column with the ID 5 is assigned as the first (index 0) available spare column.

 |
 |

sra_row

 |

`sra_row(`i`) = (`group`, `spareRowNum`, `spareRowID`)`

 |

Assign spare rows to segments: Spare row spareRowID is assigned to segment i and data bit group group as the spare number spareRowNum.

group: The data bit group to which the row belongs

spareRowNum: The index of the assigned spare row within the segment' spare columns. This can be a loop.

spareRowID: The ID of the spare row being assigned

For example: `sra_row(0) = (2,1,1)` - For segment 0 and data group 2, the spare row with the ID 1 is assigned as the second (index 1) available spare row.

 |
 |

sru_col

 |

`sru_col(`i`) = (`group`,`shareLen`, `linkLen`, `segIDs`)`

 |

Specify the usage details of spare columns: Spare column number i belongs to data bit group group, is shared by shareLen segments, links linkLen segments, and can be used to repair the segments listed in segIDs.

group: The data bit group to which the column belongs

shareLen: The number of segments that share this repair column. This can be a loop.

linkLen: The number of segments that are linked by this column, that is, that are repaired together when this column is used. This can be a loop.

segIDs: A tuple with the IDs of the segments that can be repaired using this column

For example: `sru_col(0) = (4, 2, 1, (0,1,2,3,8,9,10,11))` - Spare column 0 belongs to data bit group 4, is shared by two segments and links one segment, and can repair segments 0, 1, 2, 3, 8, 9, 10, or 11.
