|

Expressions

 |

Data types

 |
 |

operand1 + operand2

 |

Data types for the two operands can only be strings or numbers (normally signed 64 bit integers).

If both operands are strings, the result of the expression will be string.

If both operands are integers, the result of the expression will be integer.

If one operand is string and the other one is integer, the result of the expression will be string.

 |
 |

operand1 - operand2

This expression also applies to *, /, &, |, ^, <<, and >>.

 |

Data types for the two operands can only be integers (normally signed 64 bits).

The result of the expression will be integer.

 |
 |

[bit index]

 |

Data types of the bit index can only be integer.

 |
 |

operand1 > operand2

This expression also applies to >=, <, <=, and ==.

 |

Both operands must have the same data type. They can be integers, strings, or Boolean.

The result of the expression will be the Boolean type.

 |
 |

operand1 && operand2

This expression also applies to ||.

 |

Both operands can only be the Boolean type.

The result of the expression will be the Boolean type.

 |
 |

!operand

 |

The operand can only be the Boolean type.

The result of the expression will be the Boolean type.

 |
 |

~operand

 |

The operand can only be integer.

The result of the expression will be integer.

 |
 |

condition? operand1 : operand2

 |

Both operands must be the same data type. They can be integers, string, or Boolean.

If the condition is true, the value and data type of operand1 become the result of this expression.

If the condition is false, the value and data type of operand2 become the result of this expression.

 |
 |

[variable](<02.12.03.03.03.01.05_Variables.md>) = operand

 |

The value of an operand can be assigned to a variable only if they have the same data type. The possible data type can be integers, string, and Boolean.

In MTL, a variable gets its data type at its initial time, same to the initial value's data type. After that, the data type of the variable cannot be changed.

To learn more details about variable, see [Variables](<02.12.03.03.03.01.05_Variables.md>).

 |
 |

[array](<02.12.03.03.03.01.09_Array_in_MTL.md>) assignments

 |

You can assign a value to an array element only if the data types of the value and of the array are the same. The possible data type can be integers, string, and Boolean.

In MTL, an array gets its data type at the initial time, same to array element initial values' data type. After that, the data type of the array cannot be changed.

To learn more details about array assignments, see [Defining MTL arrays](<02.12.03.03.03.01.09.01.01_Defining_MTL_arrays.md>).

Keyword

Parameters and descriptions

DC_EVENT(<event>)

 .delay(<edges>)

 |

<event>: The name of the event that is to be executed. The event must be defined in the [DC event file](<02.12.03.03.08_DC_event_file.md>).

<edges>: The delay of the event, measured in waveform edges. The delay() function property is optional.

The delay is the time difference between the scheduled time of the event in the pattern and its actual execution. If the delay is negative, the event is executed before its scheduled time. The value is an expression; the expression may contain normal variables but not loop-dependent variables (that is, variables that change during a loop iteration).

The delay() property cannot be used with pmu type DC events.

The DC_EVENT function executes the specified DC event. It can be used in the [APG program file](<02.12.03.03.03_APG_program_file.md>).

 |
 |

DC_EVENT_RANGE(

 <sequence>,

 <parameters>)

 .maxRepeats(<num>)

 .initialDelay(<d>)

 {

 <instructions>

 }

 |

<sequence>: The name of the sequence that is to be executed. The event must be defined in the [DC event file](<02.12.03.03.08_DC_event_file.md>) using the :dcSequence: keyword.

<parameters>: The parameters that are passed to the sequence. Parameters are separated by commas.

<num>: The maximum number of times that the specified sequence is to be executed. The maxRepeats() function property is optional.

<d>: The amount by which the start of the sequence is delayed (relative to the beginning of the execution of the instructions in the macro body), measured in waveform edges. The initialDelay() function property is optional.

<instructions>: Standard MTL program statements. While these statements are being executed, the specified sequence is executed on the DC Scale card (subject to the limit set in maxRepeats(), if that property is used.

The DC_EVENT_RANGE function executes the specified sequence of DC events alongside the instructions in its body. It can be used in the [APG program file](<02.12.03.03.03_APG_program_file.md>).

pad(<paddingRoutine>) {}

Keyword

Parameters and descriptions

 |
 |

bitCount(<elements>, <bitState>)

 |

<elements>: The pins of the bus in question that are to be monitored. The pseudo-variable e can be used to avoid having to specify concrete pins. For example, `e[2]` refers to the second pin of the bus in the current configuration. `e[]` refers to all pins of the bus.

<bitState>: The bit state that is to be counted; either 0 or 1.

The bitCount function returns the number of bits among the specified elements that have the logical bit state given.

The function can be used for specifying the conditions of [dbi](<02.12.03.04.10_Dynamic_bus_inversion.md>) macros.

 |
 |

crc(<configuration>, <crcBit>)

 |

<configuration>: The CRC configuration that the crc macro is to use to returns the current CRC result.

<crcBit>: The bit (from the bit list specified in the CRC configuration) from which the CRC result is to be calculated.

If the pin list of the bit sequence specified in the chosen configuration includes multiple pins in each row, the result of the crc macro has multiple bits. You can access individual bits of the result using the [Select operator](<02.12.03.03.03.01.01.03_Select_operator.md>).

For example: `crc(myConfig,0)`, `crc(myConfig,0)[3]`, `crc(myConfig,0)[5,2]` (These examples assume that there is a configuration named "myConfig" in the :crc: block that is currently specified in the APG pattern file.)

The crc macro can be used in the :operation: columns of device accesses. If it is used in a device access and CRC is globally enabled, the :data: column is ignored in that access.

 |
 |

data(<d>,<x>,<y>,<z>)

 |

<d>: The unscrambled data word.

<x>: The unscrambled x address.

<y>: The unscrambled y address.

<z>: The unscrambled z address.

The data macro scrambles data words by applying the current bit inversion and bit ordering tables specified in the [APG pattern file](<02.12.03.03.02_APG_pattern_file.md>).

If fewer than four parameters are specified, the missing ones are considered to be zero. For example, `data(0xff,1)` would be the same as `data(0xff,1,0,0)`. You must specify at least two parameters.

Note that all parameters are masked with the respective device parameter from the [Device architecture file](<02.12.03.03.05_Device_architecture_file.md>), that is, dBits, xBits, yBits, and zBits. For example, when xBits is 8 and the value provided as the unscrambled x address is 258, masking would convert it to 2.

The [Select operator](<02.12.03.03.03.01.01.03_Select_operator.md>) can be applied to data macro expressions to extract one or more individual bits.

The data macro must be used on all pins for which you require [Reconstruction information](<02.12.03.04.11_Reconstruction_information.md>).

The data macro can be used in the :data: columns of device accesses.

 |
 |

dbi(<configuration>)

 |

<configuration>: The DBI configuration that the dbi macro is to use.

The dbi macro inverts the signals on a bus if a specified condition is met, as described in [Dynamic bus inversion](<02.12.03.04.10_Dynamic_bus_inversion.md>). The signal is inverted for all pins in each row in the specified DBI configuration that is completely part of the pins listed in the device access row in which the dbi macro is used. (See the DBI examples in the Examples section, below.)

Inversion is applied after scrambling; it is applied before or after cyclic redundancy checks, depending on the order in which the operations are listed with the :operationOrder: keyword.

The dbi macro can be used in the :operation: columns of device accesses. However, any device access containing the dbi macro cannot be used in padding routines.

 |
 |

xaddr(<x>,<y>,<z>)

 |

<x>: The unscrambled x address.

<y>: The unscrambled y address.

<z>: The unscrambled z address.

The xaddr macro provides the scrambled x address by applying the current scrambling table specified in the [APG pattern file](<02.12.03.03.02_APG_pattern_file.md>).

If fewer than three parameters are specified, the missing ones are considered to be zero. For example, `xaddr(1,1)` would be the same as `xaddr(1,1,0)`.

If no scrambling is specified, the macro returns the unscrambled x address.

The xaddr macro can be used in the :data: column of the device access file. The [Select operator](<02.12.03.03.03.01.01.03_Select_operator.md>) can be applied to address macro expressions to extract one or more individual bits.

 |
 |

yaddr(<x>,<y>,<z>)

 |

The yaddr macro returns the scrambled y address. It is similar to xaddr, described above.

Missing parameters are handled as follows:

- If there is only one parameter, that parameter is considered to be the unscrambled y address. For example: `yaddr(1)` is the same as `yaddr(0,1,0)`.
- If there are two parameters, they are considered to be the unscrambled x and y addresses. For example: `yaddr(1,2)` is the same as `yaddr(1,2,0)`.
 |
 |

zaddr(<x>,<y>,<z>)

 |

The zaddr macro returns the scrambled z address. It is similar to xaddr, described above.

Missing parameters are handled as follows:

- If there is only one parameter, that parameter is considered to be the unscrambled z address. For example: `zaddr(1)` is the same as z`addr(0,0,1)`.
- If there are two parameters, they are considered to be the unscrambled x and z addresses. For example: `zaddr(1,2)` is the same as `zaddr(1,0,2)`.

Keyword

 |

Parameters and descriptions

 |
 |

:bitInversion:

 |

Specifies bit inversion tables, that is, tables that tell MTL for which bits to invert logical 0 and 1 under which conditions.

This keyword is optional; it is required only if bit inversion is to be used. You need to specify bit inversion to use data scrambling.

There can be any number of :bitInversion: statements in a device architecture file. You reference the desired one from the [APG pattern file](<02.12.03.03.02_APG_pattern_file.md>) using the :bitInversion: keyword.

See the "Bit inversion keywords" table below for details.

 |
 |

:bitOrdering:

 |

Specifies bit ordering tables, that is, tables that specify ways of reordering bits.

This keyword is optional; it is required only if bit reordering is to be used. You need to specify bit ordering to use data scrambling.

There can be any number of :bitOrdering: statements in a device architecture file.You reference the desired one from the [APG pattern file](<02.12.03.03.02_APG_pattern_file.md>) using the :bitOrdering: keyword.

See the "Bit ordering keywords" table below for details.

 |
 |

:crc:

 |

Specifies a named cyclic redundancy check (CRC) setting.

This keyword is optional; it is required only if you want to use CRC.

There can be any number of :crc: statements in a device architecture file. You reference the desired one from the [APG pattern file](<02.12.03.03.02_APG_pattern_file.md>) using the :crc: keyword.

See the "CRC keywords" table below for details.

 |
 |

:dbi:

 |

Specifies a named dynamic bus inversion (DBI) setting.

This keyword is optional; it is required only if you want to use DBI.

There can be any number of :dbi: statements in a device architecture file. You reference the desired one from the [APG pattern file](<02.12.03.03.02_APG_pattern_file.md>) using the :dbi: keyword.

See the "DBI keywords" table below for details.

 |
 |

:deviceArchitecture:

 |

This keyword is required at the start of the file.

 |
 |

:deviceParam:

 |

Specifies values for device parameters, that is, the number of x, y, and (optionally) z bits and the number of data bits. You can also define custom device parameters.

See the "Device parameter keywords" table below for details.

 |
 |

:maintenanceOperation:

 |

Specifies maintenance operation (refreshes).

This keyword is optional; it is required only if a device maintenance operation is to be used.

There can be any number of :maintenanceOperation: statements in a device architecture file. You reference the desired one from the [APG pattern file](<02.12.03.03.02_APG_pattern_file.md>) using the :maintenanceOperation: keyword.

See the "Maintenance operation keywords" table below for details.

 |
 |

:operationOrder:

 |

Specifies whether dynamic bus inversion or cyclic redundancy checks should be performed first:

- To perform the DBI first, specify `{ dbi crc }`.
- To perform the CRC first, specify `{ crc dbi }`.
 |
 |

:scramble:

 |

Keyword

 |

Parameters and descriptions

 |
 |

using defaultxmode

 |

<defaultXmode>: The default [x-mode](<02.12.03.04.02_Transparent_x-modes.md>) to be used for all pins.

Supported values include:

- For normal operation: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8

You can override the default x-mode for individual pins or pin groups using the xmode pin attribute.

This parameter overrides the :xModeDefinition: parameter from the [Device access file](<02.12.03.03.04_Device_access_file.md>), if both are used. This parameter was supported in earlier versions of MTL and should no longer be used.

 |
 |

using interruptCtrl

 |

<refreshMode>: The default refresh mode for all pins that have not been assigned a mode using the interruptCtrl pin attribute (see Pin attributes, below):

VEC or VECTOR: Refreshes (maintenance operations) are triggered at runtime by counters. They occur at the next interruptible waveform (that is, a waveform with an index below 0x80) in the pattern stream.

 |
 |

using modecontext

 |

<modeContext>: The SmarTest context from the timing equation set and wavetable in which the test will be executed (see [Automatic waveform generation](<02.12.03.04.03.03_Automatic_waveform_generation.md>) for further information).

This parameter is optional; it is required for automatic waveform generation and for creating a test label.

The `using modecontext` statement overrides the :modeContext: parameter from the [APG pattern file](<02.12.03.03.02_APG_pattern_file.md>), if both are used.

 |
 |

using pinconfig

 |

<pinConfigFile>: The [Pin configuration file](<02.12.03.03.09.01_Pin_configuration_file.md>) to be used.

This parameter is optional; it is required whenever the `using port` statement is used, for example, for automatic waveform generation.

The `using pinconfig` statement overrides the :pinConfig: parameter from the [APG pattern file](<02.12.03.03.02_APG_pattern_file.md>), if both are used.

 |
 |

using port

 |

<portName>: The name of a port that is to be used for [multiport operations](<02.12.03.04.14_Multiport_operation.md>).

This keyword is optional, which is only required in multiport operations. When using "using port", you must specify the pin configuration file (see above).

You can specify multiple "using port<portName>" in your pin mapping file. However, those specified ports must not overlap with each other.

When the "using port" statement is configured in the pin mapping file, the pins which have been defined in the file but do not belong to any ports will not be compiled with vectors. During the compilation, no warnings or error messages will be issued, but error messages may show up in the Error Log view when the vector files are bing loaded in SmarTest.

 |
 |

using protocol

 |

Currently no cards use protocol-aware transaction.

 |
 |

(individual pins)

 |

<mtlPinName>: The name of the pin as it is to be used in the [Device access file](<02.12.03.03.04_Device_access_file.md>).

<refPinName>: The MTL name of a pin (called reference pin) to which the pin being defined is to be aligned. Aligning pins to reference pins is required for DC Scale pins to be mapped to specific tester cycles. See [Reference pins](<02.12.03.03.06.03_Reference_pins.md>) for details.

<smartestPinName>: The name of a SmarTest pin from the [Pin configuration file](<02.12.03.03.09.01_Pin_configuration_file.md>). This pin is mapped to the MTL pin being defined, that is, whenever the MTL pin is used in the program, the resulting waveforms are sent to the specified SmarTest pin.

<pinAtt>: An attribute for the MTL pin being defined. See the "Pin attributes" table, below, for a list of available attributes.

<attValue>: The value for the pin attribute. See the "Pin attributes" table, below, for a discussion of the values that each attribute supports.

 |
 |

(pin groups)

 |

<mtlPingroupName>: The name of the pin group as it is to be used in the [Device access file](<02.12.03.03.04_Device_access_file.md>).

<smartestPingroupName>: The name of a SmarTest pin group from the [Pin configuration file](<02.12.03.03.09.01_Pin_configuration_file.md>).

<nnn>: A three-digit number specifying an individual pin from a pin group.

<smartestPinName>: The name of a SmarTest pin from the [Pin configuration file](<02.12.03.03.09.01_Pin_configuration_file.md>). (See "individual pins", above.)

<pinAtt>: See "individual pins", above.

<attValue>: See "individual pins", above.

 |
 |

configure bus

 |

<busName>: The name of the bus as it is to be used in the [Device access file](<02.12.03.03.04_Device_access_file.md>). The name must not contain a space.

<pinList>: A list of the pin that belong to the bus. The list must contain the MTL pin names (not the SmarTest pin names); the pin names must be separated by commas.

List the pins in their bit order: The most significant bit first and the least significant bit last.

See [Buses](<02.12.03.03.06.02_Buses.md>) for details.

 |

orig:
|

Attribute

 |

Description

 |
 |

bitseq

 |

This attribute always has the value of `copy`.

This attribute-value combination causes the compiler to copy the compiled vector for the reference pin to the MTL pin, thereby speeding up the compilation process.

See [Copying vectors](<02.12.03.03.06.04_Copying_vectors.md>) for details.

 |
 |

cycleratio

 |

The ratio of the specified pin's base rate to the standard base rate. Supported ratios are `1:1`, `1:2`, and `1:4`.

If no ratio is specified, the pin ratio is `1:1`.

Pins that are used as reference pins (that is, pins that are specified in parentheses after a pin name, as described in (individual pin), above) must have a pin ratio of 1:1.

We recommend to always run DC Scale pins at a ratio of 1:4. (This requires setting up a separate port for these pins.)

When no reference pins are specified in the file, the cycle ratio is determined by the default standard base rate or default xMode.

 |
 |

exps

 |

The expansion size for the pin.

Larger expansion sizes decrease the risk of Data Queue Empty errors at the expense of requiring more vector memory. The expansion size value is proportional to the loop lengths and can range from 60 to 1,000,000.

If this attribute is set, it overrides the `-e` compiler switch (see [Starting the MTL compiler from the command line](<02.12.03.02.05_Using_the_MTL_compiler_from_the_command_line.md>)) for this pin.

 |
 |

interruptCtrl

 |

The refresh mode:

- VEC or VECTOR: Same as for the using interruptCtrl statement. (See Keywords and parameters, above.)

If the interruptCtrl attribute is not specified, the pin has the refresh mode specified by the using interruptCtrl statement. (If that statement is not present, the default is VEC.

 |
 |

type

 |

The type of the specified pin.

Currently, the types `dcscale` (for DC Scale pins) and `digital` (for standard data pins) are supported. If no pin type is specified, the type is assumed to be `digital`.

 |
 |

xmode

 |

The x-mode for this pin.

If this attribute is set, it overrides for this pin both the `using defaultxmode` statement (see above) and any :xModeDefinition: settings from the device access file.

 |
 |

system

 |

Value for it is true or false. The default value is false.

When system = true, SmarTest will generate corresponding programs for those pins (system generated). No vector data will be generated for those pins by MTP.

 |
 |

optional

 |

Value for it is true or false. The default value is false.

When optional = true, even these pins are missed in the pin configuration file, SmarTest will skip these pins and run the relative patterns without warning.

 |

|

Keyword

 |

Parameters and descriptions

 |
 |

MODECONTEXT

 |

The mode context to be used for this waveform.

This keyword is optional; it is required when WAVETBL is used and ignored otherwise.

<modeContextName>: The name of the mode context, as defined in SmarTest.

 |
 |

PINS

 |

The waveform mapping for a pin or pin group.

A waveform mapping file may contain any number of pin definitions.

<dutPinName>: A pin or pin group name defined in the pin configuration file of the SmarTest software. These names must be mapped to MTL pins in the [Pin mapping file](<02.12.03.03.06_Pin_mapping_file.md>). There can be up to 256 DUT pin names after a PINS keyword, separated by spaces. If maintenance operations are used, waveforms for non-interruptible sequences on pins in the VEC refresh mode must have indexes between (hexadecimal) 80 and FF. (See [Maintenance operations](<02.12.03.04.12_Maintenance_operations.md>) for details.)

<deviceCycleName>: This parameter should no longer be used. It was needed for [Non-transparent x-modes](<02.12.03.05.03_Non-transparent_x-modes.md>), which we recommend you no longer use. If used, it must reference a device cycle specified by the :devCyc: keyword in the [Device access file](<02.12.03.03.04_Device_access_file.md>).

The parentheses are required in any case, whether a device cycle name is given or not. (The parentheses must be omitted if the WAVETBL keyword is used.)

<waveform_specification>: A specification of the waveform. The concrete form of this specification differs according to the type of syntax, as described below.

 |
 |

WAVETBL

 |

Optional keyword.

The WAVETBL keyword is needed if a waveform mapping file is to be used for direct waveform mapping in place of a timing file.

If it is used, MODECONTEXT is also required and there must be no parentheses at the end of the PINS line. (See above.)

<wavetableName>: The name of this wavetable that can be referenced from the [APG pattern file](<02.12.03.03.02_APG_pattern_file.md>). The name can be any string complying with the [naming conventions](<02.12.03.02.03_Naming_rules_and_conventions.md>).

 |

|

Keyword

 |

Parameters and descriptions

 |
 |

:dcEvent:

 |

<eventName>: The name of a DC event.

You can give the event any desired name, as long as it follows the [naming conventions](<02.12.03.02.03_Naming_rules_and_conventions.md>).

 |
 |

:dcSequence:

 |

Defines a sequence of DC events for use by the DC_EVENT_RANGE function (described in [Macros and functions in program files](<02.12.03.03.03.01.08_Macros_and_functions_in_program_files.md>)).

A sequence of DC events can be executed concurrently to normal MTL code, allowing you to shape the voltage levels during device accesses.

DC sequences are optional; they are needed only if you want to use the DC_RANGE_EVENT function.

See the "DC sequence keywords" table below for details.

 |
 |

:dcSet:

 |

<setName>: The name of a DC event set.

You can give the set any desired name, as long as it follows the [naming conventions](<02.12.03.02.03_Naming_rules_and_conventions.md>).

A DC event file can contain any number of DC sets, although only one of them can be active at any time. The desired set is specified by name in the [APG pattern file](<02.12.03.03.02_APG_pattern_file.md>). (See the :name: keyword, below.)

 |
 |

:dcSetup:

 |

The action to be performed on the DC Scale card for the event.

<namespace>: The namespace indicates a set of DC events. It references a namespace defined in a test method or by the [DFTD](<../02.06_Command_Reference/02.06.02.02.68_DFTD__DFTD___DeFine_Test_Data.md>) firmware command.

Only one namespace can be referenced per pattern.

<dataID>: The ID of an event if the set specified by the namespace.

Note that the namespace and data ID are separated by a comma; there must be no space before or after the comma.

 |
 |

:dcTest:

 |

This keyword is required at the start of the file.

 |
 |

:name:

 |

<setName>: The name of a DC event set.

The active set for a given program is specified in the [APG pattern file](<02.12.03.03.02_APG_pattern_file.md>) using the :dcTest: keyword.

You can give the set any desired name, as long as it follows the [naming conventions](<02.12.03.02.03_Naming_rules_and_conventions.md>).

 |
 |

:pinList:

 |

<pinName>: The name of a pin (as specified in the [Pin mapping file](<02.12.03.03.06_Pin_mapping_file.md>)) affected by the event.

If multiple pins are to be affected, separate their names by commas. Do not add spaces after the commas or enclose the entire pin list in quotes. You cannot specify pin groups.

You can specify [Buses](<02.12.03.03.06.02_Buses.md>) defined in the [Pin mapping file](<02.12.03.03.06_Pin_mapping_file.md>).

For PMU events (see :type:, below), you can also specify ports.

 |
 |

:type:

 |

The pin type.

Two types of events are available:

- pmu: The event controls the PMUs of standard pins. Note that DC events of this type cannot be used in event sequences.
- DCScale: The event controls pins on DC Scale cards.
 |

|

Name

 |

Description

 |
 |

mapConverterProperties

 |

The top-level element. It has two attributes:

- xmlns:xsi: This must always be "http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
- xsi:NoNameSpaceSchemaLocation: is the location of the schema file for the device configuration file. By default, the file is named propertyFileAPI.xsd and is located in the same directory as the Automatic map Converter binary.

Technically, these attributes could be omitted, but this would prevent any validation of the file. We recommend including these attributes and using an XML editor to edit the file to ensure syntactical correctness.

 |
 |

deviceSetup

 |

The path to the MTL pattern file (.apg). The path can be absolute or relative to the device directory and is stored in the patternFile attribute.

 |
 |

coordinateDependency

 |

This element contains the specification of the addressing scheme of the device.

It has no attributes.

 |
 |

geomAddr

 |

The geomAddr element describes how the geometric x- and y-coordinates map to rows and columns of the device.

- rowCol: This attribute can contain either "xy" or "yx".

"xy" specifies that x-coordinates correspond to rows and y-coordinates to columns.

"yx" specifies that x-coordinates correspond to columns and y-coordinates to rows.

 |
 |

level

 |

The level elements specify the order of significance of the address dimensions: The outermost level element specifies the most significant dimension, the next level element, the next significant dimension, and the innermost element the least significant dimension.

There is one attribute:

- coordinate: This attribute specifies the address dimension.

Supported values are: "DQ", "bank", and "row/col".

The coordinate value for the outermost level element must always be either "DQ" or "Bank".

 |
 |

matrix

 |

matrix elements specify the numbering and orientation properties of banks, DQs and segments.

At the top level of the mapConverterProperties element, there must be one matrix element for banks and one for DQs; in other words, there must be exactly two matrix elements.

In the redundancyAnalysis element, there must be exactly one matrix element, which describes the arrangement of segments.

A matrix element has one attribute:

- type: This attribute specifies the address dimension being described.

If the matrix element is at the top level of the mapConverterProperties element, type can have the values "DQ" or"bank".

If the matrix element is located within a redundancyAnalysis element, type must have the value "segment".

 |
 |

dimensions

 |

The number of rows and columns into which these banks or DQ areas are organized:

- rows: The number of rows
- cols: The number of columns
 |
 |

layout

 |

The layout element contains the numbering and orientation for each bank or DQ area.

It has no properties of its own but contains one cell element for each row/column combination.

 |
 |

cell

 |

A cell element describes the numbering and orientation for one bank or DQ area.

It has these attributes:

- col: The column value of the bank or DQ area being described
- row: The row value of the bank or DQ area being described
- id: The number by which this bank or DQ area is referred to.
- xOrient: The direction in which the row addresses in this bank or DQ area grow. Possible values are "down" (larger x-values indicate addresses further down) or "up" (larger x-values indicate addresses further up).

The xOrient attribute is omitted when the cell element is located within a redundancyAnalysis element.

- yOrient: The direction in which the column addresses in this bank or DQ area grow. Possible values are "right" (larger y-values indicate addresses further right) or "left" (larger y-values indicate addresses further left).

The yOrient attribute is omitted when the cell element is located within a redundancyAnalysis element.

Note that the orientation specified for one address dimension also affects all less significant address dimensions. If the orientation is redefined for a less significant dimension, the effective orientation for the cells is a superimposition of both definitions.

For example, if memory cells are specified first by bank and then by DQ and the xOrient value for both dimensions is "up", the resulting orientation for the cells is "down".

 |
 |

redundancyAnalysis

 |

The redundancyAnalysis element contains information that the Automatic Map Converter needs to create the get_ra_layout and phys_to_layout function, which are required for redundancy analysis.

This element is optional. If it is missing, the two functions are not generated.

 |
 |

COLS_IN_BLPAIR

 |

This element describes the number of columns in a bit line pair of the device.

The number is contained in the value attribute.

 |
 |

ROWS_IN_WLSET

 |

This element describes the number of rows in a word line set of the device.

The number is contained in the value attribute.

 |
 |

BLPAIRS_PER_SEGM

 |

This element describes the number of bit line pairs per segment of the device.

The number is contained in the value attribute.

 |
 |

WLSETS_PER_SEGM

 |

This element describes the number of word line sets per segment of the device.

The number is contained in the value attribute.

 |

For single-port testing:

`{spec_name_0}; {spec_name_1}; ...; {spec_name_n-1}`

spec_name_0, spec_name_1, ... , spec_name_n-1 are names of specification variables.

`{spec_name_0@port_0}; {spec_name_1@port_1}; ...; {spec_name_n-1@port_n-1}`

 |

 |

Number. The ending value for the sweep. The unit is nanoseconds.

 |
 |

MinOpenEye

 |

Number. The step size of the linear search, specified in nanoseconds. For the sweep to deliver useful results, this must be considerably smaller than the expected minimum eye open time. The unit is nanoseconds.

AlignAccuracy

 |

Number. The resolution (end criterion) of the binary search, specified in nanoseconds.

 |
 |

PrintEye

 |

Yes or No. If Yes output is printed to the report window.

EdgeCentering

 |

Yes or No. If Yes, the edge center timing data in the sweep spec var is used for further measurements in the later test suite.

Parameter

mode

 |

Measurement mode. It can be: TM::GPF (default), TM::PPF, TM::PVAL, or TM::DCTEST_AUTO.

- TM::GPF: This mode executes a global pass/fail measurement. The test will pass if all of the measurements pass. The test result can be retrieved with the getPassFail() member function.
- TM:PPF: This mode executes a per-pin pass/fail measurement. The pass/fail result for each measured pin can be retrieved with the `getPassFail(const STRING & pinlist)` member function. In this mode, you can also retrieve the global pass/fail result with the getPassFail() member function.
- TM::PVAL: This mode executes a per-pin value measurement. The result value for each measured pin can be retrieved with the getValue(const STRING & pin) member function. In this mode, you can also retrieve the global pass/fail result and the per-pin pass/fail result by using the getPassFail() and getPassFail(const STRING & pinlist) member function, respectively.
- TM::DCTEST_AUTO: This mode executes the DC test according to the test suite flags.

If the flag ["Pass value"](<../02.08_Setup_and_Result_Tools/02.08.04.32.01.02.07.01_Alphabetical_list_of_flags.md#_342556__row_value_on_pass>) or ["Fail value"](<../02.08_Setup_and_Result_Tools/02.08.04.32.01.02.07.01_Alphabetical_list_of_flags.md#_342556__row_value_on_fail>) is on, the DC test will execute in the same way as in the TM::PVAL mode.

If the flags "Pass value" and "Fail value" are off and the flag ["Per pin on pass"](<../02.08_Setup_and_Result_Tools/02.08.04.32.01.02.07.01_Alphabetical_list_of_flags.md#_342556__row_per_pin_on_pass>) or ["Per pin on fail"](<../02.08_Setup_and_Result_Tools/02.08.04.32.01.02.07.01_Alphabetical_list_of_flags.md#_342556__row_per_pin_on_fail>) is on, the DC test will execute in the same way as in the TM::PPF mode.

If the flags "Pass value" and "Fail value" are off and the flag "Per pin on pass" and "Per pin on fail" are off, the DC test will execute in the same way as in the TM::GPF mode.

The default value is TM::GPF.

Parameter

Description

name

 |

A string to name the generated bit fail map files.

The name string can contain application model variables, testflow variables, and the reserved variables listed below to display more information in the file name, such as wafer, site, and port information. The syntax for using a variable in the name is ${variable name}.

- ${time}: The file name will show the time at which the BFD file is generated.
- ${pattern}: The file name will show the name of the memory pattern (per pin subroutines generated by the MTL compiler) that the BFD file is generated from.
- ${label}: The file name will show the name of the start label where in the pattern to start generating the BFD file.
- ${port}: The file name will show the name of the port that the pattern belongs to.
- ${site}: The file name will show the site number.
- ${test}: The file name will show the name of the test suite.

If the name string contains a variable which is an application model variable and that is also a testflow variable, the file name will display the value of the application model variable.

If the name string does not contain a variable, all generated BFD files will have the same name and the later one will overwrite the earlier one.

If the string does not contain the ${time} variable, the BFD file generated with the execution of a test and the BFD file generated with RA if you have [enabled RA](<02.12.06.17.31_MTP_MEMORY_TEST.setRAEnablingMode.md>) and configured [setRAEndAction(MTP::RA_END_SAVE_BFD)](<02.12.06.17.32_MTP_MEMORY_TEST.setRAEndAction.md>) will have the same name. The later one will overwrite the earlier one.

By default, all generated BFD files are saved to: device/mts/bitmap/bitmap_data. You can change the path of BFD files generated with an execution of a test by using [MTP_MEMORY_TEST.setBitMapFilePath()](<02.12.06.17.16_MTP_MEMORY_TEST.setBitMapFilePath.md>) or [MTP_MEMORY_PATTERN.setBitMapFilePath()](<02.12.06.15.02_MTP_MEMORY_PATTERN.setBitMapFilePath.md>). But you cannot change the path of the BFD file generated with RA.

Examples:

- "${time}-${label}-${pattern}-Port${port}-Site${site}"
- "Time${time}-Port${port}-$Lot{LOT_ID}-Cassette${CASSETTE_ID}-Wafer${WAFER_ID}-X${DIE_X}-Y${DIE_Y}"
 |

Parameter

 |

Description

 |
 |

name

 |

A string to name the generated BFD files. The name string can contain application model variables, testflow variables, and the reserved variables listed below to display more information in the file name, such as wafer, site, and port information. The syntax for using a variable in the name string is ${variable name}.

- ${time}: The file name will show the time at which the BFD file is generated.
- ${pattern}: The file name will show the name of the memory pattern (per pin subroutines generated by the MTL compiler) that the BFD file is generated from.
- ${label}: The file name will show the name of the start label where in the pattern to start generating the BFD file.
- ${port}: The file name will show the name of the port that the pattern belongs to.
- ${site}: The file name will show the site number.
- ${test}: The file name will show the name of the test suite.

If the name string contains a variable which is an application model variable and that is also a testflow variable, the file name will display the value of the application model variable.

If the name string does not contain a variable, all the BFD files will have the same name and the later one will overwrite the earlier one.

If the string does not contain the ${time} variable, the BFD file generated with the execution of a test and the BFD file generated with RA if you have [enabled RA](<02.12.06.17.31_MTP_MEMORY_TEST.setRAEnablingMode.md>) and configured [setRAEndAction(MTP::RA_END_SAVE_BFD)](<02.12.06.17.32_MTP_MEMORY_TEST.setRAEndAction.md>) will have the same name. The later one will overwrite the earlier one.

By default, all generated BFD files are saved to: device/mts/bitmap/bitmap_data. You can change the path of the BFD file generated with an execution of a test by using [MTP_MEMORY_TEST.setBitMapFilePath()](<02.12.06.17.16_MTP_MEMORY_TEST.setBitMapFilePath.md>). But you cannot change the path of the BFD file generated with RA.

Examples:

- "${time}-${label}-${pattern}-Port${port}-Site${site}"
- "Time${time}-Port${port}-$Lot{LOT_ID}-Cassette${CASSETTE_ID}-Wafer${WAFER_ID}-X${DIE_X}-Y${DIE_Y}"

If any of the specified data bits or banks exceeds limit, the overall test result is fail. Data bits or banks that are not included in entity do not cause a fail when they exceed limit failed bits.

This parameter is optional. If it is not specified, all data bits or all banks are compared to limit, unless an index has been specified. (That is, the default value is "@".)

Specifying an index for an element (data bit or bank) is the same as specifying a list containing only the name of that element as the entity.

- `setFBCLimit(MTP::FBC_DBIT,4,2)`

The kind of training to be performed.

For possible values, see the TrainingType definition in the [CSearchTask](<02.12.06.31.02_CSearchTask.md>) class.

 |
 |

trainingAlgorithm

 |

The training mode to be used:

- Full training searches for both edges of the data eye and calculates the center of the eye from these edges. Any values specified in the PinOffsets parameter are added to the position of the first edge to find the starting value for searching for the second edge.
- Fast training searches only for the first edge of an eye. The center of the eye is calculated by adding the PinOffsets value to the position of this edge.

We recommend that you use the constants defined in the [CSearchTask](<02.12.06.31.02_CSearchTask.md>) class.

 |
 |

edgeCentering

 |

Yes (Spec), Yes (Pin attr), Yes (Embedded), or No. Whether and how to use the edge center timing value for further measurements:

- Yes (Spec): Centering by setting spec values is performed.
- Yes (Pin attr): Centering by setting pin attributes is performed.
- Yes (Embedded): Centering is done in the test head card. The method used is similar to the one the SmarTest [EyeFinder](<02.12.02.05.06.04_EyeFinder.md>) uses.
- No: No further centering is performed.

If this parameter is set to Yes (Pin attr), the unit for the sweep spec variables must be nanoseconds.

If the training algorithm is EmbeddedTraining, only the values Yes (Embedded) and No are available for this parameter.

We recommend that you use the constants defined for the various settings (see the Constants section in Class definition in [CSearchTask](<02.12.06.31.02_CSearchTask.md>)) for specifying this value.

setupPinList

resultPinList

<list of pin groups>. List of data output result pins or pin groups, separated by semicolons. Each group consists of one or more pins separated by commas. The number of data output pin groups must be equal to the number of address pin groups.

 |

sweepSpecsList

<list of variable names>. List of timing spec variables for the setup pin groups specified above, one variable per pin group. For example: `A0_ADDRtrng, A1_ADDRtrng`. The number of timing specification variables must be equal to the number of pin groups.

For multiport timing, add @port to the variable name. Or, set the DefaultPort parameter (below) to `@`.

If the EdgeCentering value is Yes (Pin attr), the unit for the SweepSpecVars values must be nanoseconds.

 |
 |

sweepStartList

 |

<number or list of numbers>. The starting point of the specification search.

The unit is the same as the unit specified in the timing equation for the sweep specification variable.

There are different ways of specifying the sweep start values:

- If you specify only one value, it applies to all setup pins.
- If you specify a list of values separated by commas, each applies to one pin group only. In this case, the number of sweep start values must be the same as the number of pin groups.
- To specify a sweep start for a particular pin group, enter <number>`@`<pin_group>. A mixture of <number> and <number>`@`<pin_group> notation is possible; in this case, the single value applies to all pin groups, except for those for which an individual value has been specified.

If you do not specify a number, the sweep starts at -4 test system periods from the expected location of the edge.

 |
 |

sweepStopList

 |

<number or list of numbers>. The ending point of the specification search.

The syntax is the same as for SweepStart, above.

If you do not specify a number, the sweep ends at 12 test system periods after the expected location of the edge.

 |
 |

minOpenEye

 |

<number>. The step size in nanoseconds for the linear search. The specified time must be significantly shorter than the minimum eye open time.

A value of 0 results in the default being used (1/10 of the device cycle).

 |
 |

alignAccuracy

 |

<number>. Specify the resolution of the binary search in nanoseconds.

A value of 0 results in the default being used (1/100 of the device cycle).

 |
 |

sweepType

Absolute or Relative. Which values to use for the sweep:

- Absolute: The sweep begins at SweepStart and ends at SweepStop.

 |

 |
 |

--noEDL

 |

 |
 |

--numberOfDummyRuns <integer>

 |

This parameter specifies the number of initial testflow executions that will not be included in the test time measurement. 0 is allowed. The default is 1.

The total number of executions is

numberOfDummyRuns + numberOfRuns.

By default, this is 21.

 |
 |

--numberOfRuns <integer>,

-n <integer>

 |

By default, the testflow is executed 20 times for test time measurements. This number does not include the first execution of the testflow (and eventual further dummy runs), which usually takes much longer than the following runs.

 |
 |

--outdir <output_directory>,

-o <output_directory>

 |

By default, the TTT tool uses the report subdirectory of the current device as its output directory. With this parameter, you can select another output directory.

 |
 |

--password <password>,

-p <password>

 |

This parameter specifies the password to be used for returning to Engineering mode. The default is "engineer".

 |
 |

--pause

 |

When this option is selected, the TTT tool pauses before each testflow execution to allow switching the device in the socket.

 |
 |

--selectSiteForSingleSite <site_number>

 |

By default, site 1 is used to measure the single site test time. With this parameter, you can select another site.

This parameter is ignored if --skipSingleSite is also specified.

 |
 |

--selectSitesForMultiSite <site_string>

 |

By default, all sites are enabled in order to measure multi-site test time. With this parameter you can restrict the number of site to be taken into account.

For example if you specify

--selectSitesForMultiSite 1001

then only site 1 and 4 will be enabled.

This parameter is ignored if --skipMultiSite is also specified.

 |
 |

--skipEclipseRestart

 |

With this option, the TTT tool stays in supervising mode after the test times are measured. This is mainly needed for scripting purposes so the TTT can be run multiple times in succession without restarting Eclipse between the different runs.

 |
 |

--skipEclipseShutdown,

-e

 |

By default, the TTT tool switches to Supervisor mode before it starts test time measurement. If this flag is set test times will be measured in Engineering mode.

 |
 |

--skipFormatter

 |

By default, the report formatter .default.PROD is used. If you specify this flag, the formatter is not changed.

 |
 |

--skipMultiSite

 |

If this flag is set, multi-site test time will not be measured. The --selectSitesForMultiSite parameter will be ignored.

 |
 |

--skipSingleSite

 |

If this flag is set, single site test time will not be measured. The --selectSiteForSingleSite parameter will be ignored.

 |
 |

--skipTestTimes,

-s

 |

This flag suppresses collection of test times. It is equivalent to --skipMultiSite and --skipSingleSite combined.

 |
 |

--stdf

 |

If this flag is set, STDF files will be copied to the log directory.

 |
 |

--switchOnCallgrind,

-v

 |

This flag switches on Callgrind measurement after preliminary executions.

 |
 |

--tag <string>

 |

This parameter specifies a string that is appended to the automatically generated name of the log directory. The format of this name is

`ttt_<YYYYMMDD>_<HH>h<MM>m<SS>s`

For example, if you specify

--tag example

the directory name will end with example.

 |
 |

--version

 |

If this flag is set, the TTT tool displays version information and exits.

 |

Error case

 |

Symptoms

 |

Root Cause

 |

User Action

 |
 |

1

 |

Diagnostics or calibration identifies a pin as defective.

 |

Front-end failure, but test processor is okay.

 |

Add defective channel to MCDIgnore file (see MCDIgnore file in Service_Guide Part 1). Restart SmarTest. Channel is marked as unavailable. Disable site on handler. Loading the pin configuration will automatically disable the site the channel of which is defect.

 |
 |

2

 |

Diagnostics, calibration and pin configuration report "channel unavailable".

 |

Test processor is defective.

 |

Disable site on handler. Load pin configuration.

 |
 |

3

 |

Software fails with sequencer timeout of a channel.

 |

Test processor fails during test.

 |

If the failing channel is known, add it to the MCDIgnore file (see MCDIgnore file in Service_Guide Part 1). Disable the site on the handler. Exit SmarTest and start it again. Loading the pin configuration disables sites with defective channels.

 |
 |

4

 |

All tests fail on one site.

 |

Front-end failure (including contact failures).

 |

Disable the site using the site control window. Disable the site on the handler. Continue testing.

 |

|

 |

Description

 |
 |

Protocol

  ![Protocol icon](<../../../../raw/126129.png>) |

A [Protocol](<../../02_System_reference/02.07_Test_Method_Reference/02.07.11.01.09.10_Protocol.md>)describes the signaling in respect of timing, level and message format which is required to exchange information between the sender and receiver of an interface.

It is defined in the protocol editor.

 |
 |

Transaction

  ![Transaction icon](<../../../../raw/126130.png>) |

The protocol describes different [transactions ](<../../02_System_reference/02.07_Test_Method_Reference/02.07.11.01.09.13_Transaction.md>)to exchange information between the sender and receiver of the interface. Typical transactions are read and write.

Transactions usually have parameters, which are used within UTM for passing values to or receiving values from the DUT.

One transaction can utilize one or multiple pin roles which reflect the (device independent) interface to the DUT.

Transactions sometimes also referred to as frame.

They are defined in the protocol editor.

 |
 |

Field

  ![Field icon](<../../../../raw/126132.png>) |

Each transaction is build out of one or several [fields ](<../../02_System_reference/02.07_Test_Method_Reference/02.07.11.01.09.03_Field.md>)which describe the logical structure of the transaction.

Fields are associated with pin roles used in the transaction.

They are defined in the protocol editor.

 |
 |

 |

 |
 |

Pin role

  ![Pin role icon](<../../../../raw/126131.png>) |

A [Pin role](<../../02_System_reference/02.07_Test_Method_Reference/02.07.11.01.09.08_Pin_role.md>) is the abstract (device independent) definition of an interface pin of a protocol. For instance, MDC and MDIO are typical pin names (roles) of the MDIO protocol.

It is associated with a physical device pin in the protocol assignment.

Pin roles are defined in the protocol editor.

 |
 |

Protocol assignment

  ![Protocol assignment icon](<../../../../raw/128197.png>) |

[Protocol assignment](<../../02_System_reference/02.08_Setup_and_Result_Tools/02.08.04.18.03.10_Protocol_assignments.md>) is the central point where device independent definitions (the protocol and its pin roles) are mapped (assigned) to the resources of the tester (physical pins via ports).

The protocol assignment can be opened from via the Test Program Explorer.

 |
 |

 |

 |
 |

Encoding

 |

[Encoding ](<../../02_System_reference/02.07_Test_Method_Reference/02.07.11.01.11.04_Encoding_functions.md>)defines how to convert a transaction into state characters, respectively vectors.

Encoding at field level is mandatory to convert and execute transactions during test.

Encode definitions are entered in the protocol editor.

 |
 |

Decoding

 |

[Decoding ](<../../02_System_reference/02.07_Test_Method_Reference/02.07.11.01.11.05_Decoding_function.md>)defines how to extract transaction's parameter values from vectors, respectively state characters.

Decoding is optional. When omitted, vectors cannot be translated back to parameter values of transactions. Thus a transaction may not display its parameters in the pattern editor properly.

Decode definitions are entered in the protocol editor.

 |
 |

 |

 |
 |

Specific protocol definition tabs

 |

The protocol editor provides separate tabs for entering protocol specific timing, level, wavetable/state map details. These details will be saved with the protocol definition.

This way they can be imported with the protocol definition to another device.

 |
 |

timing

 |

The syntax of [protocol specific timing](<../../02_System_reference/02.08_Setup_and_Result_Tools/02.08.04.22.10.09_Editing_protocol_specific_timing.md>) is equivalent to the device timing definition.

For implementing a protocol's timing segment to the device timing equation, manually add the line:

USE_PROTOCOL"<protocolName>:<timingSegmentName>" [<PortList>]

 |
 |

levels

 |

The syntax of [protocol specific levels](<../../02_System_reference/02.08_Setup_and_Result_Tools/02.08.04.22.10.07_Editing_protocol_specific_levels.md>) is equivalent to the device level definition.

For implementing a protocol's level segment to the device level equation manually add the line:

USE_PROTOCOL"<protocolName>:<levelSegmentName>" [<PortList>]

 |
 |

wavetable & state map

 |

The syntax of the [wavetable/state map](<../../02_System_reference/02.08_Setup_and_Result_Tools/02.08.04.22.10.08_Editing_protocol_specific_wavetable_and_state_map.md>) is equivalent to the device wavetable.

 Note Where multiple timing/level segments can be used per protocol, only one unique wavetable/state map is allowed!

For implementing the protocol's wavetable/state map to the device wavetable file manually add the line:

USE_PROTOCOL"<protocolName>" [<PortList>]

 |
